title: Determinant of order two
zh: 二阶行列式定义

blocks.text: We begin with the determinant of order two.
Definition. The determinant of a two-by-two array is defined by the following formula.
板书：写二阶行列式及展开式。sub 表示下标；这里竖线表示行列式。
Let me write the formula on the board. The vertical bars denote a determinant. We read the right-hand side as: a sub one one times a sub two two, minus a sub one two times a sub two one.

title: Determinant of order three
zh: 三阶行列式定义

blocks.text: Next, we define the determinant of order three.
Definition. The determinant of a three-by-three array is the following sum of six signed products.
Each product uses one entry from each row and each column. The first three products have plus signs. The last three have minus signs. We will define the general sign rule after studying permutations.
板书：写六项；每项是相乘，项之间是 plus 或 minus。three-by-three 读 three by three。§1中的二元、三元解公式统一由后面的克拉默法则证明。

title: Permutations and parity
zh: 定义1—3

blocks.text: Next, we define permutations, inversions, and parity.
Definition 1. A permutation of order n is an arrangement of 1 to n, with each number used exactly once. The arrangement 1, 2, ..., n is the natural order.
指向排列：这里连写表示顺序，不是相乘。
We write a permutation as j sub one, j sub two, through j sub n. The braces show that these entries are exactly the numbers from one to n.
Definition 2. An inversion is a pair in which the larger entry comes first. The inversion number is the number of these pairs.
读法：tau 读 /taʊ/；# 表示个数；括号后的冒号表示满足后面的条件。
We denote the inversion number by tau. Here, the hash symbol means the number of elements in the set. We count pairs of positions p and q, where p is less than q and j sub p is greater than j sub q.
Definition 3. A permutation is even or odd according as its inversion number is even or odd.
≡ 读 is congruent to；mod 2 读 modulo two。
We write this using congruence modulo two. A remainder of zero means even; a remainder of one means odd.
The natural order is therefore even. We use the same definitions for any n distinct natural numbers.
Counting formula. There are n factorial permutations of order n.
Proof
There are n choices for the first position. There are n minus one choices for the second. Continue until one choice remains. Multiplying the numbers of choices gives n factorial.

title: Transpositions
zh: 对换定义

blocks.text: We now define a transposition.
Definition. A transposition exchanges two entries and fixes all other entries. It is adjacent when the two entries are next to each other.
板书：写出对换前后；箭头说明交换，不必逐字读省略号。
Here, s is the number of entries between j and k. The arrow shows that we exchange j and k. All the entries in between keep their positions.

title: A transposition changes parity
zh: 定理1及证明

blocks.text: The first theorem describes how a transposition changes parity.
Theorem 1. A transposition changes an even permutation into an odd permutation, and an odd permutation into an even permutation.
π 读 pi /paɪ/；π′ 读 pi prime。先指原排列，再指新排列。
Let pi denote the original permutation, and pi prime the new one. In this notation, tau of pi prime is congruent to tau of pi plus one, modulo two.
Proof

First, suppose j and k are adjacent. Every other entry is before both or after both. Its inversion pairs with j and k stay the same. Pairs containing neither entry also stay the same. Only the pair j, k changes.
Δτ 读 delta tau；分段公式按两个 if 句读。
Delta tau means the new inversion number minus the old one. It is minus one if j is greater than k, and plus one if j is less than k.
So an adjacent transposition changes the parity.
Now suppose s entries lie between j and k. The following adjacent transpositions exchange j and k and leave all other entries in place.

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}\cdots j\,i_1\cdots i_s\,k\cdots&\xrightarrow{s+1}\cdots k\,j\,i_1\cdots i_s\cdots\\&\xrightarrow{s}\cdots k\,i_1\cdots i_s\,j\cdots.\end{aligned}

blocks.text: 板书：保留原书的两步变换；指箭头上的次数。
The numbers above the arrows count adjacent transpositions: s plus one first, then s more.
Each adjacent transposition changes parity. The number of transpositions is odd, so the final parity changes. This completes the proof.

title: Equal numbers of even and odd permutations
zh: 推论及证明

blocks.text: Next, we introduce a corollary of Theorem One.
Corollary. For n at least 2, there are equally many even and odd permutations of order n. Each number is n factorial divided by 2.
denotes 表示“表示、记作”；# 的读法已在定义2说明。
Here, s denotes the number of odd permutations, and t denotes the number of even permutations.
n! 读 n factorial；≥ 读 is greater than or equal to。
We read this as: s equals t equals n factorial divided by two, for n greater than or equal to two.
Proof

Let s be the number of odd permutations and t the number of even permutations. Swap the first two entries in each odd permutation. By Theorem One, each result is even. The results are distinct, since swapping again recovers the original permutation. Therefore, there are at least s even permutations.
Now start with the even permutations and do the same thing. We obtain t distinct odd permutations. Therefore, there are at least t odd permutations.
The two inequalities give s equals t. There are n factorial permutations in total, so each number is n factorial divided by two.

title: Sorting by transpositions
zh: 定理2及证明

blocks.text: We now state Theorem Two.

Theorem 2. Every permutation can be changed into natural order by finitely many transpositions, and conversely. The number of transpositions is even for an even permutation and odd for an odd permutation.
接下来已有的英文句子读同余式；m 与逆序数奇偶性相同。
On the board, m denotes the number of transpositions. The arrow takes the permutation to natural order.
m is congruent to tau of pi modulo two.
Proof: existence
We use induction on n. For n equal to one, no transposition is needed. Assume every permutation of order n minus one can be sorted.
If the last entry is n, sort the first n minus one entries by the induction hypothesis. Leave n fixed.
If the last entry is not n, swap it with n. Then use the previous case. This completes the induction. Reversing the transpositions gives the reverse transformation.
j′ 读 j prime；带下标时如 j sub one prime。
The primes mark the entries after the transposition. They do not mean derivatives here.
Proof: parity
Each transposition changes parity. After m transpositions, we reach the natural order, whose inversion number is zero. Hence the original inversion number plus m is even.
The reverse sequence has the same length. This proves both directions.

title: Determinant of order n
zh: 定义4

blocks.text: We can now define the determinant of order n.

Definition 4. For entries in a number field P, the determinant is the sum of products choosing one entry from each row and each column. In increasing row order, a product has a plus sign for an even column permutation and a minus sign for an odd one.
板书：A 是矩阵，aᵢⱼ 是元素；n×n 读 n by n；aᵢⱼ∈P 读 a sub i j belongs to P。
Let A be an n by n matrix. We write a sub i j for the entry in row i and column j. Here, P is the number field from which we choose the entries. We read the membership symbol as belongs to.
板书：指 D、det A 和竖线行列式，说明三者是同一个数。
We denote its determinant by D, or det A. We read det A as the determinant of A.
完整读法：D equals the sum over all permutations j sub one through j sub n, of minus one raised to tau of that permutation, times a sub one, j sub one, through a sub n, j sub n。乘积中每个 a 有行、列两个指标。

Let me write the defining sum. D equals the sum over all column permutations. Each term is minus one raised to the inversion number of the column permutation, times the product of the selected entries.
The sum runs over all permutations of 1 to n. The first index is the row index; the second is the column index.

title: Triangular determinants
zh: 三角行列式结论及证明

blocks.text: We next state the triangular determinant result.

Definition. The main diagonal consists of the entries a sub i i. An array is upper triangular if all entries below its main diagonal are zero. It is diagonal if all entries off the main diagonal are zero.
> 读 is greater than；≠ 读 is not equal to。
In symbols, a sub i j equals zero when i is greater than j. For a diagonal matrix, it equals zero whenever i is not equal to j.
Result. An upper triangular determinant equals the product of its diagonal entries.
板书：指对角元素的乘积，不用逐项展开所有因子。
The right-hand side is a sub one one times a sub two two, and so on, times a sub n n.
Proof

Consider a term that is not zero. Its last-row entry must be a sub n n. Column n is now used. In row n minus one, we must therefore choose column n minus one. Continuing upwards forces every column index to equal its row index.
All other terms are zero. The diagonal term has the natural column order, so its sign is plus. If a diagonal entry is zero, this term is zero too. The formula still holds.
Corollary. A diagonal determinant is the product of its diagonal entries. If all diagonal entries are 1, its value is 1.
diag(d₁,…,dₙ) 可直接读 the diagonal matrix with entries d sub one through d sub n；Iₙ 读 I sub n。
Here, diag means the diagonal matrix with entries d sub one through d sub n. I sub n denotes the identity matrix of order n.
Proof
A diagonal array is upper triangular. Apply the result just proved.

title: Sign of a term in any order
zh: 一般项符号及证明

blocks.text: Next, we state the sign rule for factors written in any order.
Result. For a product choosing one entry from each row and each column, its coefficient in the determinant is minus one to the sum of the row and column inversion numbers.

blocks.latex: a_{i_1j_1}\cdots a_{i_nj_n},\qquad i_1\cdots i_n,\ j_1\cdots j_n\text{ are permutations}

blocks.text: aᵢ₁ⱼ₁ 可读 a sub i sub one, j sub one；口述用 row … and column … 更清楚。
In each factor, the first index gives the row and the second gives the column. For example, the first factor is the entry in row i sub one and column j sub one.
指指数中的两个 τ：分别对应行指标排列和列指标排列。
We read the sign as: minus one raised to the sum of the two inversion numbers.
Proof
Swap factors until the row indices are in natural order. Theorem Two shows that this is possible. Changing the factor order does not change the product.
Each exchange of two factors gives one transposition of the row indices and one of the column indices. By Theorem One, both inversion numbers change parity. Their sum keeps the same parity.
The final row inversion number is zero. The sign is therefore the sign of the final column permutation, exactly as in the definition.
This proves the rule.

title: Column order and transpose
zh: 按列公式、转置性质及证明

blocks.text: This sign rule gives the formula in column order.
Result. In increasing column order, the sign of each term is determined by the row permutation.
板书：指 aᵢ₁₁ 到 aᵢₙₙ，列指标依次为1到n。
Here, the columns are in natural order, and the sum runs over all row permutations.
Proof
Write each product in increasing column order. This lists the same products once each. The column inversion number is zero, so the general sign rule gives this formula.
We now define the transpose and state Property One.
Definition. Transposing an array exchanges its rows and columns.
Aᵀ 读 A transpose；bᵢⱼ=aⱼᵢ 读 b sub i j equals a sub j i。
We denote the transpose of A by A transpose. Its entry in row i and column j is a sub j i.
Property 1. Transposing an array does not change its determinant.
指转置前后的两个行列式。
This says: the determinant of A transpose equals the determinant of A.
Proof
Write the determinant of B in column order. Replace each entry of B by the corresponding entry of A. The result is the row-order definition of the determinant of A.

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}\det B&=\sum_{i_1\cdots i_n}(-1)^{\tau(i_1\cdots i_n)}b_{i_1 1}\cdots b_{i_n n}\\&=\sum_{i_1\cdots i_n}(-1)^{\tau(i_1\cdots i_n)}a_{1i_1}\cdots a_{ni_n}\\&=\det A.\end{aligned}

blocks.text: Definition. An array is lower triangular if all entries above its main diagonal are zero.
Corollary. A lower triangular determinant equals the product of its diagonal entries.
Proof
Its transpose is upper triangular and has the same diagonal entries. Apply Property One and the upper triangular formula. This completes the proof.

title: Scaling one row
zh: 性质2及零行推论

blocks.text: We now continue with the determinant properties. We state them for rows. By Property One, they also hold for columns.
Property 2. Multiplying one row by a number k multiplies the determinant by k.
板书：写完整行列式，指出改变的第i行；不引入整行简写。
On the left, every entry in row i is multiplied by k. On the right, k is outside the determinant.
Proof
Fix row i. Each term contains exactly one entry from this row. Group the terms by this entry and factor it out.
区分小写 aᵢⱼ 与大写 Aᵢⱼ。后面紧接原稿对系数含义的说明。
We write the coefficients with a capital A. The first term is lowercase a sub i one times capital A sub i one.
Here A sub i j is the sum left after factoring out a sub i j from its group. It contains no entry from row i. So these coefficients stay the same when row i changes.
Using this expression, we get
Corollary. If all entries in one row are zero, the determinant is zero.
Proof
Set k equal to zero in Property Two.

title: Splitting one row
zh: 性质3及证明

blocks.text: Next, we state Property Three.
Property 3. If each entry in one row is a sum of two numbers, the determinant splits into two determinants. All other rows stay the same.
板书：其余各行照写；分别指左边的一行和右边对应的两行。
Let me write the three determinants. In the changed row, the entries are b sub j plus c sub j. On the right, we separate the b entries and the c entries.
Proof
Let this be row i. Use the same coefficients A sub i j, which do not depend on this row. Expand and separate the two sums.
This proves Property Three.

title: Two equal rows
zh: 性质4及证明

blocks.text: We now state Property Four.
Property 4. If two rows are equal, the determinant is zero.
板书：这是两行对应元素相等，i、k 是两个不同的行号。
In symbols, a sub i j equals a sub k j for every j from one to n. Here, i is not equal to k.
Proof
Suppose rows i and k are equal. By the definition, the determinant is

blocks.latex: \begin{vmatrix}a_{11}&a_{12}&\cdots&a_{1n}\\\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots\\a_{i1}&a_{i2}&\cdots&a_{in}\\\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots\\a_{k1}&a_{k2}&\cdots&a_{kn}\\\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots\\a_{n1}&a_{n2}&\cdots&a_{nn}\end{vmatrix}=\sum_{j_1\cdots j_n}(-1)^{\tau(j_1\cdots j_i\cdots j_k\cdots j_n)}a_{1j_1}\cdots a_{ij_i}\cdots a_{kj_k}\cdots a_{nj_n}

blocks.text: We show that all terms cancel in pairs. For each term, the following term also occurs:

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}&(-1)^{\tau(j_1\cdots j_i\cdots j_k\cdots j_n)}a_{1j_1}\cdots a_{ij_i}\cdots a_{kj_k}\cdots a_{nj_n},\\&(-1)^{\tau(j_1\cdots j_k\cdots j_i\cdots j_n)}a_{1j_1}\cdots a_{ij_k}\cdots a_{kj_i}\cdots a_{nj_n}.\end{aligned}

blocks.text: aᵢⱼᵢ 可以说 the entry in row i and column j sub i；aₖⱼₖ 同理。
Compare the factors from rows i and k. In the second term, their column indices are exchanged.
Since the two rows are equal, we have
So the products are equal. The two column permutations differ by one transposition:

blocks.latex: j_1\cdots j_i\cdots j_k\cdots j_n,\qquad j_1\cdots j_k\cdots j_i\cdots j_n

blocks.text: Their signs are opposite, so these two terms cancel. Every term has a distinct partner, and exchanging again returns the original term. Thus all terms cancel in pairs.

title: Two proportional rows
zh: 性质5及证明

blocks.text: Next, we obtain Property Five.
Property 5. If two rows are proportional, the determinant is zero.
指 aᵢ₁,…,aᵢₙ 与 kaᵢ₁,…,kaᵢₙ 两行。
In this determinant, each entry in one row is k times the corresponding entry in the other row.
Proof
By Property Two, take the common factor k out of one row. The two rows are then equal, so Property Four gives zero.

title: Adding a multiple of another row
zh: 性质6及证明

blocks.text: Next, we state Property Six.
Property 6. Adding a multiple of one row to another row does not change the determinant.
板书：指第i行的和，再指保持不变的第k行；i 与 k 不同。
On the left, the new entry in row i and column j is a sub i j plus c times a sub k j. Row k stays the same. The determinant on the right is the original one.
Proof
By Property Three, split row i into two parts. The second determinant has two proportional rows, so it is zero by Property Five.
This completes the proof.

title: Exchanging two rows
zh: 性质7及证明

blocks.text: Property Six gives us one more result. We now state Property Seven.
Property 7. A transposition of two rows changes the sign of the determinant.
板书：写交换第i行与第k行后的完整行列式。i 与 k 不同；其余行不变。
Here, we exchange rows i and k. The new determinant equals minus the original determinant. Changing the sign means multiplying the value by minus one.
Proof
We use Property Six three times. First, add row k to row i. The determinant stays the same.
第一步：第i行变成两行之和，第k行不变。
Next, subtract the new row i from row k. Row k becomes the negative of the original row i.
第二步：使用刚更新的第i行。每个元素 a sub k j minus the sum of a sub i j and a sub k j，结果为 minus a sub i j。
Now add the new row k to row i. Row i becomes the original row k.
第三步：两行之和加上原第i行的相反数，留下原第k行。
Finally, factor minus one out of row k, by Property Two.
factor minus one out of row k：从第k行提出公因子−1。这里第k行指当前位置。
The rows are now exchanged. So the original determinant is minus the exchanged determinant. This proves Property Seven. By transposing, the same result holds for two columns.

title: Example 1: Two types of entries
zh: 例1 对角元为a、其余为b

blocks.text: We now apply these properties to two examples. Let us begin with Example One.
Example 1. Calculate the determinant of order n whose diagonal entries are a and whose other entries are b.
板书：写出完整行列式。省略号表示同样的规律延续，不必逐个读 dot。
We denote this determinant by lowercase d. Each row contains one a and n minus one entries equal to b.
Solution
First, add columns two through n to column one, one at a time. By Property Six for columns, the determinant does not change. Every entry in the first column becomes a plus n minus one times b.
columns two through n：第二列到第n列。a+(n−1)b 读 a plus the quantity n minus one times b。只改变第一列。
Next, factor a plus n minus one times b out of the first column, by Property Two.
提出公因子，不是除以公因子；即使 a+(n−1)b=0，这个等式也成立。
Now subtract the first row from each of rows two through n. The remaining determinant becomes upper triangular.
subtract the first row from …：从……减去第一行。竖线内仍是行列式；外面的方括号只把公因子括在一起。
Its diagonal entries are one, followed by n minus one copies of a minus b. Multiply these diagonal entries to get the result.
结果读法：d equals the quantity a plus n minus one times b, multiplied by the quantity a minus b raised to the power n minus one。
This completes the calculation.

title: Example 2: An odd-order skew-symmetric determinant
zh: 例2 奇数阶反对称行列式

blocks.text: Next, we consider Example Two. We first define a skew-symmetric determinant.
Definition. A determinant is skew-symmetric if each entry is the negative of the entry in the transposed position.
We read this as: a sub i j equals minus a sub j i, for i and j from one to n.
Example 2. Prove that a skew-symmetric determinant of odd order is zero.
Proof
First, take i equal to j. Each diagonal entry is its own negative, so it is zero.
板书：先写全零主对角线，再写上方元素及下方相反数。skew-symmetric 读 /skjuː sɪˈmetrɪk/。
By Property One, transposing the determinant does not change its value. This gives
Now factor minus one out of every row of the transposed determinant. By Property Two, the total factor is minus one to the power n. The remaining determinant is the original one.
factor minus one out of every row：每一行都提出−1，总共有n个因子。(-1)ⁿ 读 minus one to the power n。
Therefore, d equals minus one to the power n times d. Since n is odd, d equals minus d. Hence d is zero.
This completes the proof.

title: Matrices and elementary operations
zh: 定义5—6 · 矩阵与初等变换

blocks.text: We now introduce matrices and elementary operations.
Definition 5. An s-by-n matrix over P is a rectangular array of s n entries from P, arranged in s rows and n columns. A square matrix has the same number of rows and columns.
We read s by n as the size of the matrix. The entry a sub i j is in row i and column j. Parentheses denote the matrix. For a square matrix, vertical bars denote its determinant, which is a number.

Definition 6. The elementary row operations are: multiply a row by a nonzero scalar; add a scalar multiple of one row to another; exchange two rows. The corresponding operations on columns are elementary column operations.

blocks.latex:
egin{aligned}a_{ij}&\longmapsto k a_{ij}&& (k
e0;\ j=1,\ldots,n),\a_{ij}&\longmapsto a_{ij}+c a_{\ell j}&& (i
e\ell;\ j=1,\ldots,n),\(a_{ij},a_{\ell j})&\longmapsto(a_{\ell j},a_{ij})&& (i
e\ell;\ j=1,\ldots,n).\end{aligned}

blocks.text: Here, the arrow means that we replace each indicated entry. In the second operation, row ell stays fixed. All other rows stay fixed as well. For column operations, we make the same changes down a column.
scalar 是数域P中的数；ℓ 读 ell。必须强调第一类变换的 k 非零。矩阵变换用箭头，不把两个不同矩阵写成相等。
We use this arrow to say that elementary operations change A into B. It does not mean that A and B are equal.

title: Row echelon form
zh: 阶梯形与行列式计算

blocks.text: Definition. A matrix is in row echelon form if its zero rows are at the bottom, and the first nonzero entry of each nonzero row is to the right of the first nonzero entry of the row above it.
The first nonzero entry in a row is called a leading entry. In this pattern, the leading entries are in columns two and four. Every entry below a leading entry is zero.
Result. Every matrix can be changed into row echelon form by elementary row operations.
Proof

If the matrix is zero, it is already in echelon form. Otherwise, find the first column with a nonzero entry. Exchange rows to put a nonzero entry at the top. Suppose this is the first column, and write the new top-left entry as a prime sub one one.

For each lower row i, subtract a prime sub i one divided by a prime sub one one times the first row. This clears the first column below the leading entry. Now repeat on the remaining rows and columns to the right. Skip any column that is zero in the remaining rows. Each step fixes one more leading entry, so the process stops in echelon form.
a′ᵢⱼ 读 a prime sub i j；这里撇号表示换行后的元素。边指第一列边说明消元系数；无需逐项读整个矩阵。

Determinant calculation. A square echelon matrix is upper triangular. Its determinant is the product of its diagonal entries. The original determinant is recovered by tracking row scalings and row exchanges.
Justification

A row addition leaves the determinant unchanged. A row exchange changes its sign. Scaling a row multiplies the determinant by the scale factor. All scale factors used in elementary operations are nonzero. Collecting these factors gives k. The triangular determinant formula then gives the displayed result.

title: Minors and cofactors
zh: 定义7—8 · 余子式与代数余子式

blocks.text: Next, we define minors and cofactors. These describe expansion along a row or column.
Definition 7. The minor M sub i j of an entry a sub i j is the determinant obtained by deleting row i and column j, keeping the remaining rows and columns in their original order.
We denote this minor by capital M sub i j. It has order n minus one. At an edge, the rows or columns before or after the deleted position may be absent.
Definition 8. The cofactor of a sub i j is its minor multiplied by minus one to the power i plus j.
Capital A sub i j denotes the cofactor. Lowercase a sub i j denotes the original entry. The sign is positive when i plus j is even, and negative when it is odd.
minor 余子式；cofactor 代数余子式。读法：capital A sub i j equals minus one to the power i plus j, times capital M sub i j。
Result. Grouping the determinant terms by their entry in row i gives coefficients equal to these cofactors.
Proof

Each determinant term contains exactly one entry from row i. Group the terms according to this entry. Its coefficient depends only on the other rows. To find the coefficient of a sub i j, replace row i by zeros, except for a one in column j. Call the resulting determinant E. Then E is exactly that coefficient.
Move row i to the bottom using n minus i adjacent row exchanges. Then move column j to the last position using n minus j adjacent column exchanges. Keep the order of all the other rows and columns.
In the defining sum, the last row must contribute its last entry, one. Appending the last column index n creates no inversion. The remaining sum is exactly M sub i j.
The two exponents differ by an even number, so the signs agree. This identifies the coefficient and proves the formula.

title: Expansion along a row or column
zh: 定理3 · 展开与交叉乘积和

blocks.text: We can now state the full expansion theorem.
Theorem 3. The sum of the entries in a row times their own cofactors equals the determinant. Using the cofactors of a different row gives zero. The corresponding statements hold for columns.

In the first formula, the entries come from row k and the cofactors from row i. Read the sum as: the sum from s equals one to n of a sub k s times capital A sub i s. The second formula uses columns ell and j.
分段读 equals D if k equals i, and zero otherwise。大写A是代数余子式，不是元素；先说明指标属于哪一行或列。
Proof
The case k equals i is the expansion formula just proved. Now let k be different from i. Replace row i by row k. Its cofactors stay the same, because their minors delete row i.
The two displayed copies occupy rows i and k. The determinant is zero because these rows are equal. Transpose the determinant to obtain the column formulas. This completes the proof.

title: The Vandermonde determinant
zh: 范德蒙德行列式及证明

blocks.text: Result (Example 2). The Vandermonde determinant equals the product of all differences a sub i minus a sub j with j less than i.

The large product symbol means multiply all the indicated factors. We read the right-hand side as: the product of a sub i minus a sub j, over all pairs with one less than or equal to j, less than i, less than or equal to n.
Vandermonde 可读 van-der-MOND；∏ 读 the product。各列由同一个数的零次到n−1次幂组成。
Proof

We use induction on n. For n equal to two, the determinant is a sub two minus a sub one. Suppose the formula holds for order n minus one. Starting at the bottom, subtract a sub one times the preceding row from each row.
Working upwards makes sure that the preceding row still has its original entries. Expand along the first column. Factor a sub j minus a sub one out of each remaining column j.

The remaining determinant has order n minus one. By induction, it supplies all differences involving only a sub two through a sub n. The factors outside supply all differences involving a sub one. Together they give the required product.
Corollary. A Vandermonde determinant is zero if and only if at least two of the numbers are equal.
Proof
A product of numbers in P is zero exactly when one factor is zero. Here, a factor is zero exactly when two of the numbers are equal.

title: A determinant with a zero corner
zh: 零角块行列式及证明

blocks.text: Result (Example 3). If the upper-right rectangular part of a determinant is zero, the determinant is the product of the two square determinants on the diagonal.
The square parts have orders k and r. The entries below the first square can be arbitrary.
Proof

We use induction on k. If k is one, expansion along the first row gives a sub one one times the second determinant. Suppose the result holds when the first square has order k minus one. Expand along the first row. Only its first k entries can contribute.
Every minor still has a zero upper-right part. Apply the induction hypothesis to each minor and take out the common determinant formed by the b entries.
The bracket is the first-row expansion of the determinant formed by the a entries. This proves the result.
板书保留各元素；括号内是小行列式的按第一行展开，不能把求和遗漏。

title: Cramer’s rule
zh: 定理4 · 克拉默法则

blocks.text: We now use determinants to solve a square linear system.

Theorem 4 (Cramer’s rule). A system of n linear equations in n unknowns has a unique solution if its coefficient determinant d is nonzero. Its j-th unknown equals d sub j divided by d, where d sub j replaces column j by the constant terms.
Read the solution as: x sub j equals d sub j divided by d. In d sub j, only column j is replaced. We prove existence first, then uniqueness.
Cramer’s rule 克拉默法则；coefficient determinant 系数行列式。用手指替换列。下面Aᵢⱼ始终是原系数行列式的代数余子式。
Proof: existence
Write the i-th equation as a sum. Expand d sub j along its replaced column. Its cofactors are unchanged, so we obtain the following formula.
Substitute d sub j divided by d. Exchange the order of the two finite sums. Then apply Theorem Three.
The inner sum is d when s equals i, and zero otherwise. Thus every equation is satisfied. A solution exists.
Proof: uniqueness
Let c sub one through c sub n be any solution. Multiply equation i by the cofactor capital A sub i k, and add all equations.
On the left, exchange the sums. The column version of Theorem Three leaves only the term with j equal to k.
This holds for every k. Every solution must equal the one already found, so it is unique.

title: Homogeneous square systems
zh: 定理5 · 齐次方程组

blocks.text: Definition. A linear system is homogeneous if all its constant terms are zero. The solution with all entries zero is the zero, or trivial, solution. Any other solution is a nonzero, or nontrivial, solution.
Nonzero means that at least one component is nonzero. It does not mean that every component is nonzero.

Theorem 5. A homogeneous system of n equations in n unknowns has only the zero solution if its coefficient determinant is nonzero. Therefore, a nonzero solution requires the coefficient determinant to be zero.
Proof
In Cramer’s rule, every replaced column is zero. Hence every d sub j is zero. Dividing by the nonzero determinant gives the unique zero solution.
homogeneous 齐次；trivial solution 零解。此处只证明必要条件；第三章再证明逆命题。

title: Complementary minors and their signs
zh: 定义9—10 · 子式及其代数余子式

blocks.text: We now extend expansion from one row to several rows.

Definition 9. A minor of order k is formed by choosing k rows and k columns in their original order. For k less than n, deleting these rows and columns gives its complementary minor of order n minus k.
Definition 10. The cofactor of this minor is its complementary minor multiplied by minus one to the sum of all selected row and column indices.
We read M prime as the complementary minor. Here, capital A is the cofactor of the whole minor M. It is a number. The indices in the exponent are the positions in the original determinant.
Lemma. Every term in the expanded product M A is a term of the original determinant, with the same sign.
Proof
First suppose M is the upper-left minor of order k. Its cofactor is M prime, because twice the sum from one to k is even. Choose one term from each minor.

Every beta index is larger than every alpha index. There are no inversions between the two parts. The total inversion number is the sum of the two internal inversion numbers. Thus the product has exactly the sign of the corresponding determinant term.
α alpha，β beta。后半段减k只是把其数值改成1到n−k，大小关系不变。
For a general minor, move its selected rows to the first k positions, in order. Then do the same with its columns. The numbers of adjacent exchanges are the following.
Let D one denote the new determinant. The total sign is minus one to the sum of the selected indices, since twice the sum from one to k is even.
In D one, the product M M prime has the correct term signs by the first case. Returning to D multiplies all signs by the displayed factor. That factor turns M M prime into M A. The lemma follows.

title: Laplace expansion
zh: 定理6 · 拉普拉斯定理

blocks.text: Theorem 6 (Laplace expansion). Fix k rows of an n-order determinant, where one is at most k and k is less than n. The determinant is the sum of every minor using these rows times its cofactor. The same statement holds for k fixed columns.
The subscript labels a choice of k columns. There are n choose k such choices. Each M sub ell uses the fixed rows and one of these column choices. Capital A sub ell is its cofactor.
binomial coefficient 二项式系数，读 n choose k；t 表示选取方式的个数。
Proof

By the lemma, every term on the right occurs in D with the correct sign. Two different choices of columns cannot give the same term: the entries in the fixed rows use different sets of columns. It remains to count the terms.

Each minor contributes k factorial terms. Each cofactor contributes n minus k factorial terms. The total is n factorial, exactly the number of terms in D. Thus every term is counted once. Transposition gives expansion along fixed columns.

title: Multiplication of determinants
zh: 定理7 · 行列式乘法法则

blocks.text: Theorem 7. The product of two n-order determinants equals the determinant whose entry in row i and column j is the sum of the products of row i of the first array and column j of the second array.
We multiply corresponding entries from row i and column j, and add. Capital C denotes the resulting determinant.
Proof
Form the following determinant of order two n. Its upper-right part is zero, and the lower-left part has minus one on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere.
Expand along the first n rows by Laplace’s theorem. Only the first n columns give a possibly nonzero minor. Its cofactor has positive sign. Hence D equals D one times D two.

Now add a sub i one times row n plus one, through a sub i n times row two n, to row i. Do this for each i from one to n. These are row additions, so the determinant is unchanged. The first n entries in each top row become zero. Its last n entries become the corresponding c entries.
Expand again along the first n rows. Only the last n columns can contribute. Their cofactor contains the diagonal determinant with n entries equal to minus one.
The total exponent is two n times n plus one, which is even. Therefore, D one times D two equals C. This completes the proof.

title: Linear systems and elementary transformations
zh: 方程组与定义1 · 初等变换

blocks.text: We now study general linear systems. The numbers of equations and unknowns need not be equal.
First, we define solutions and equivalence of linear systems.

Definitions. A solution of a linear system is an ordered list of values that satisfies every equation. The solution set contains all solutions. Two systems are equivalent if they have the same solution set.

Here, s is the number of equations and n is the number of unknowns. A solution is a list of n values, in the order of the unknowns. The coefficient a sub i j belongs to equation i and unknown j. All coefficients, constants, and solution entries are taken in P.
Next, we introduce the three elementary transformations of a linear system.
Definition 1. Elementary transformations of a linear system are: multiply an equation by a nonzero number; add a multiple of one equation to another; exchange two equations.
Result. Every elementary transformation preserves the solution set.
Proof

To prove that an elementary transformation preserves solutions, we must prove both inclusions of solution sets. First check that every old solution satisfies the transformed equations. Then use the inverse transformation to recover every old equation from the new system.
Consider adding k times the second equation to the first. A solution of the original system satisfies both equations below.
Multiply the second equality by k and add it to the first. This gives the new first equation. All other equations stay the same.

Conversely, subtract k times the unchanged second equation to recover the original first equation. Thus the two systems have the same solutions. Multiplication by a nonzero number is reversed by division by that number. Exchanging equations is reversed by exchanging them again. These operations also preserve all solutions.
We now introduce the augmented matrix, which records both the coefficients and the right-hand sides.
Definition. The augmented matrix contains the coefficients and one additional column of constant terms.
We denote the augmented matrix by A bar. Elementary transformations of equations are exactly elementary row operations on this matrix.
augmented matrix 增广矩阵；A bar 读A上方横线。最后一列也必须参与每次行变换。

title: Elimination and free unknowns
zh: 消元法 · 一般解与自由未知量

blocks.text: Elimination result. Reduce the augmented matrix by row operations. A row with all coefficients zero and a nonzero constant means no solution. Otherwise, if there are r leading entries, the system has a unique solution when r equals n and infinitely many solutions when r is less than n.
The vertical separator only separates coefficients from the constant term. It is not a determinant symbol. We now prove the remaining cases.
Proof

We must distinguish a contradiction from a consistent system. In the consistent case, the number of leading entries determines how many unknowns are fixed by back substitution and how many can be chosen freely. We will explain both the unique-solution and the infinitely-many-solutions cases.

Apply the row reduction from Chapter Two. Each row operation preserves solutions. We can relabel the unknowns so the leading unknowns are x sub one through x sub r. Remove equations that say zero equals zero. If there is no contradiction, the remaining system has this form.
If r equals n, start with the last equation and solve upwards. Each diagonal coefficient is nonzero, so each step gives exactly one value. This is back substitution.
If r is less than n, first choose arbitrary values for x sub r plus one through x sub n. Move their terms to the right. Back substitution then determines the other values uniquely.
Next, we define free unknowns and the general solution.
Definitions. Unknowns that can be assigned arbitrary values are free unknowns. Formulas expressing all solutions in terms of them form a general solution.

There are n minus r free unknowns. Different choices give different solutions. Since P contains infinitely many numbers, there are infinitely many solutions. If r is zero and there is no contradiction, every unknown is free.
free unknowns 也常说 free variables；back substitution 回代。i=n−1,…,1 是倒序，读 from n minus one down to one。
Theorem 1. A homogeneous system with fewer equations than unknowns has a nonzero solution.
Proof

Assume the system is homogeneous and the number of equations is less than the number of unknowns. We must find a solution with at least one nonzero entry. In echelon form, there cannot be more leading entries than equations, so at least one unknown is free. We will assign one free unknown a nonzero value.

A homogeneous system always has the zero solution. After elimination, the number r of leading entries cannot exceed s. Thus r is less than n, so at least one unknown is free. Give one free unknown the value one. The resulting solution is nonzero.

title: Vectors and vector operations
zh: 定义2—7 · 向量及运算

blocks.text: Next, we introduce vectors to describe relations among equations.
We now introduce vectors and their components.
Definition 2. An n-dimensional vector over P is an ordered list of n numbers in P. These numbers are its components.
We denote a vector by a Greek letter, such as alpha. We read its components as a sub one, a sub two, through a sub n. Their order matters.
Next, we define equality of vectors.
Definition 3. Two vectors are equal if all corresponding components are equal.
We now define vector addition.
Definition 4. The sum of two vectors is formed by adding their corresponding components.
Next, we introduce the zero vector and the negative of a vector.
Definition 5. The zero vector has every component zero. The negative of a vector has the negative of each component.
We use this negative vector to define subtraction.
Definition 6. Vector subtraction means addition of the negative vector.
Finally, we define multiplication of a vector by a scalar.
Definition 7. Scalar multiplication multiplies every component of a vector by the same number from P.
We read k alpha as k times alpha. The number k is the scalar. All these operations are performed component by component.
α alpha，β beta，γ gamma。零向量在原书中也记0，由上下文区别数0。

title: Vector laws and n-dimensional vector space
zh: 运算规律与定义8

blocks.text: All vectors in these identities have the same number of components, and all scalars belong to P. To prove a vector equality, we must show equality in each component. We can then use the corresponding addition and multiplication laws in the number field.

Vector laws. Addition is commutative and associative, zero is an additive identity, and every vector has an additive inverse. Scalar multiplication satisfies the two distributive laws, associativity of scalar factors, and multiplication by one.
These are the eight basic rules. The first two allow us to change the order and grouping of addition. The next two describe zero and negatives. The last four describe scalar multiplication.
Verification

Equality of vectors is equality of all components. In each component, the first two identities say that addition of numbers is commutative and associative. The next two say a plus zero equals a, and a plus minus a equals zero. For the last four, the component identities are these.
These hold in the number field P. Therefore, the vector identities hold.
Consequences. Zero times a vector is zero; minus one times a vector is its negative; any scalar times the zero vector is zero. A nonzero scalar times a nonzero vector is nonzero.
Verification
The first three formulas follow directly from their components. For the last, choose a nonzero component of alpha. Multiplying it by nonzero k gives a nonzero component of k alpha.
We now name the set equipped with these operations: the n-dimensional vector space over P.
Definition 8. The n-dimensional vector space over P consists of all n-component vectors over P, together with the addition and scalar multiplication just defined.
A vector can be written as a row or as a column. The component order is the same; only its layout changes.
commutative 交换的；associative 结合的；distributive 分配的。讲解时指相应等式，不必重复朗读所有下标。

title: Linear combinations and equivalent systems of vectors
zh: 定义9—10 · 线性组合与等价

blocks.text: First, we introduce linear combinations. We begin with one vector and a given system of vectors, all with the same number of components over the same number field P.

Definition 9. Let beta sub one through beta sub s be vectors over P. If there are scalars k sub one through k sub s in P such that alpha equals their linear combination, then alpha is called a linear combination of beta sub one through beta sub s. We also say that alpha can be expressed linearly in this system.
We also say alpha can be expressed linearly in beta sub one through beta sub s. The numbers k sub one through k sub s are the coefficients.
Textbook example: expressing one vector
The book returns to the vectors coming from the earlier system of equations. Multiply alpha sub one by three and subtract alpha sub two. Compare the four components.
Thus alpha sub three is a linear combination of alpha sub one and alpha sub two, with coefficients three and minus one.
Unit vectors. The n unit vectors each have a single component equal to one, in the indicated position, and zeros elsewhere. Every n-component vector is their linear combination.

We read epsilon sub i as the unit vector with one in position i. The equality follows by comparing components. The zero vector is a linear combination of any nonempty system: take every coefficient zero.
Next, we introduce linear expression for a whole system and then equivalence of two systems. We must check every vector in the first system, not just one of them.

Definition 10. Let alpha sub one through alpha sub t and beta sub one through beta sub s be two systems of vectors over P with the same number of components. If, for each i from one through t, the vector alpha sub i can be expressed as a linear combination of beta sub one through beta sub s, then we say that the system alpha sub one through alpha sub t can be expressed linearly in the system beta sub one through beta sub s. The two systems are called equivalent if each can be expressed linearly in the other.

For each fixed i, we need one such expression. The coefficients may change with i. To prove equivalence, we also need an expression for every beta vector in terms of the alpha vectors. The two systems need not have the same number of vectors.
Textbook example: two equivalent systems
First, express each alpha vector in the beta system. Adding beta sub one and beta sub two gives alpha sub one. Adding beta sub one and twice beta sub two gives alpha sub two.
This proves one direction. For the reverse direction, subtract the first equality from the second to obtain beta sub two. Then subtract beta sub two from alpha sub one to obtain beta sub one.
We have now expressed every vector of either system in the other system. Therefore the two systems are equivalent.

Transitivity of linear expression. If the alpha system can be expressed linearly in the beta system, and the beta system can be expressed linearly in the gamma system, then the alpha system can be expressed linearly in the gamma system.
Proof of transitivity of linear expression

Assume that the first system has t vectors, the second has s vectors, and the third has p vectors. Our first assumption gives coefficients k sub i j for each alpha vector. Our second assumption gives coefficients ell sub j m for each beta vector. All these coefficients belong to P.
Our goal is to express each alpha sub i using only gamma sub one through gamma sub p. Fix i. In its expression, replace every beta sub j by the expression supplied by the second assumption.
Now collect all terms multiplying the same gamma sub m. These are finite sums, so we may change their order. The coefficient of gamma sub m is the sum, over j, of k sub i j times ell sub j m.

Each new coefficient is a sum of products of elements of P, so it is also in P. We have obtained the required expression for alpha sub i. Since i was arbitrary, it holds for every alpha vector. This proves transitivity.
Reflexivity. Every system of vectors is equivalent to itself.
Proof of reflexivity
To express a given vector of the system, give that vector coefficient one and give every other vector coefficient zero. This works for each vector in the system.
Thus the system can be expressed linearly in itself. The two directions required by equivalence are the same in this case.
Symmetry. If the alpha system is equivalent to the beta system, then the beta system is equivalent to the alpha system.
Proof of symmetry

Assume the alpha and beta systems are equivalent. By Definition Ten, every alpha vector is a linear combination of the beta vectors, and every beta vector is a linear combination of the alpha vectors. Reading these same two conditions in the opposite order gives precisely the definition of equivalence of the beta system to the alpha system.
Transitivity of equivalence. If the alpha system is equivalent to the beta system and the beta system is equivalent to the gamma system, then the alpha system is equivalent to the gamma system.
Proof of transitivity of equivalence

Assume both stated equivalences. For the first direction, the alpha system is expressible in the beta system and the beta system in the gamma system. The transitivity just proved expresses the alpha system in the gamma system. For the reverse direction, the gamma system is expressible in the beta system and the beta system in the alpha system. Applying the same result again expresses the gamma system in the alpha system. Both directions hold, which proves equivalence.
equivalent 等价；reflexive 自反；symmetric 对称；transitive 传递。这里“向量组等价”不等于向量逐个相等。
先分别写出两条已知的线性表出，再说明目标；“线性表出的传递性”先证明一次，“等价的传递性”须把这个结论正反各用一次。教材例子的双向系数在此展开，便于口述核对。

title: Linear dependence and independence
zh: 定义11、11′、12及等价证明

blocks.text: Next, we introduce the definition of linear dependence. We ask whether one vector in a system can already be expressed using the other vectors.
Definition 11. A system of at least two vectors is linearly dependent if one vector is a linear combination of the others.
The dependent vector need not originally be the last one. We place it last only to simplify the notation. The other coefficients may be zero.
Textbook examples of linear dependence

The three vectors from the preceding example form a dependent system because alpha sub three is expressed by the other two. Also, a system of at least two vectors containing the zero vector is dependent: express that zero vector using coefficient zero on every other vector. For two vectors, dependence means that at least one is a scalar multiple of the other.

For geometric vectors in three-dimensional real space, the book interprets dependence using lines and planes through the origin. Two vectors are dependent exactly when both lie on such a line. Three are dependent exactly when they lie in such a plane. If two of the three are independent, they determine the plane and the third is a combination of them. If no two are independent, the system is already dependent. Zero vectors are included in these statements.
We now give an equivalent definition using a homogeneous vector equation. This version also applies to a system containing just one vector.
Definition 11 prime. A system of one or more vectors is linearly dependent if a linear combination with coefficients not all zero equals the zero vector.
Not all zero means that at least one coefficient is nonzero. We now show that these definitions agree for two or more vectors.
Proof of equivalence

There are two implications to prove. First assume the original definition: one of the vectors is a linear combination of the others. We must construct a zero combination whose coefficients are not all zero.
If one vector is expressed in the others, move it to the left. Its coefficient is minus one, so the coefficients are not all zero.
The coefficient list is k sub one through k sub s minus one, followed by minus one. Whatever the other coefficients are, the last coefficient is nonzero. This proves the first implication.

For the reverse implication, assume a zero combination with coefficients not all zero. We must isolate one vector as a combination of the remaining vectors. At least one coefficient is nonzero; after relabelling, call it k sub s.
Conversely, take a relation with coefficients not all zero. Relabel so that k sub s is nonzero. Divide by it and solve for alpha sub s.
Thus one vector is a linear combination of the others. The definitions agree.
Finally, we introduce linear independence, which excludes all such nontrivial zero combinations.
Definition 12. A system is linearly independent if the zero vector can be obtained as a linear combination only when every coefficient is zero.
This is the negation of linear dependence. We read the arrow as implies. The distinction is whether a nonzero list of coefficients can give the zero vector.
linearly dependent 线性相关；linearly independent 线性无关。不要把“向量和等于零”直接当作相关，必须检查系数不全为零。
“a nonzero solution”指系数向量不为零，即至少一个系数非零；不是每个系数都非零，也不是要求原来的向量非零。

title: Basic consequences of independence
zh: 部分组、添加分量与方程组判别

blocks.text: Result 1. A system containing a dependent subsystem is dependent. Equivalently, every nonempty subsystem of an independent system is independent.
Proof

For the first result, assume a subsystem is dependent. Our target is a nontrivial zero combination of the full system. Keep the known coefficients on that subsystem and assign coefficient zero to every added vector. At least one of the original coefficients remains nonzero.

Start with a dependence relation in the subsystem. Give coefficient zero to each added vector. The coefficients are still not all zero, so the full system is dependent. The second statement is the contrapositive.
Result 2. A single vector is dependent exactly when it is zero. The unit vectors are linearly independent.
Proof
If k alpha is zero and k is nonzero, divide by k to get alpha equal to zero. Conversely, one times the zero vector is zero. For the unit vectors, compare the components below.
Result 3. Independence of a system of vectors is equivalent to its associated homogeneous system having only the zero solution.
Proof
A vector equality holds exactly when every component equality holds. These component equalities are the displayed equations. A nonzero solution is exactly a dependence relation.
Result 4. Adding components to each vector of an independent system preserves independence.
Proof

A zero linear combination of the new vectors gives a zero linear combination of the old vectors when we read the first n components. The old vectors are independent, so every coefficient is zero. Repeating this argument allows any number of added components.
associated homogeneous system 中未知量是线性组合系数；原向量按列进入系数矩阵，不要把i、j位置颠倒。

title: Comparing two systems of vectors
zh: 定理2及三个推论

blocks.text: We now compare the numbers of vectors in two systems. Let the alpha system contain r vectors and the beta system contain s vectors, all over the same number field and with the same number of components.

Theorem 2. Assume the following two conditions: first, every vector alpha sub one through alpha sub r can be expressed linearly in beta sub one through beta sub s; second, r is greater than s. Then the system alpha sub one through alpha sub r is linearly dependent.

The first condition gives the displayed expressions. The second compares the number r of alpha vectors with the number s of beta vectors. The scalars t sub j i are fixed coefficients in these expressions: the first index identifies the beta vector, and the second identifies the alpha vector. We do not assume that the beta vectors are independent.
Proof

Let us first state exactly what we must prove. By the definition of linear dependence, we need scalars k sub one through k sub r, not all zero, whose linear combination of the alpha vectors is zero. In other words, the following homogeneous vector equation must have a nonzero solution.

Here a nonzero solution means at least one k is nonzero. To find these scalars, temporarily write the unknown coefficients as x sub one through x sub r. We will call a chosen solution k sub one through k sub r. Substitute the known expression for each alpha vector into their linear combination.

For each beta sub j, collect its contributions from all r alpha vectors. This gives the coefficient t sub j one times x sub one, through t sub j r times x sub r. In summation notation, the same calculation is

To make this vector zero, it is sufficient to make every displayed coefficient of beta equal to zero. We use this as a sufficient condition; without independence of the beta vectors, it is not necessarily a necessary condition. We therefore solve the following scalar homogeneous system.

There is one equation for each beta vector, so there are s equations. The unknowns are x sub one through x sub r, so there are r unknowns. The second hypothesis says r is greater than s. Theorem One therefore guarantees a solution with these r entries not all zero.
Now use this particular solution as the coefficients of the alpha vectors. Each coefficient of beta in the collected expression vanishes.
We have produced a zero combination of the alpha vectors with coefficients not all zero. This is exactly the proof target, so the alpha system is linearly dependent.
证明顺序：两条假设 → 目标k₁α₁+⋯+kᵣαᵣ=0且系数不全为零 → 设未知数xᵢ → 代入αᵢ的表达式 → 按βⱼ合并 → s个方程、r个未知数 → 取非零解代回。此处沿教材用r记α向量个数。
Corollary 1. If r independent vectors can be expressed linearly in s vectors, then r is at most s.
Proof

Assume the alpha system is independent and expressible in the beta system. We want to prove r is at most s. Suppose instead that r is greater than s. Both hypotheses of Theorem Two would then hold, so the alpha system would be dependent. This contradicts the assumption and proves the inequality.
Corollary 2. Any n plus one vectors with n components are linearly dependent.
Proof

Take any n plus one vectors with n components. Every one is a linear combination of the n unit vectors. Thus the first condition of Theorem Two holds with the given vectors as the alpha system and the unit vectors as the beta system. The second condition holds because n plus one is greater than n. The given system is therefore dependent.
Corollary 3. Two equivalent independent systems contain the same number of vectors.
Proof

Let the two independent systems contain r and s vectors. Equivalence gives linear expression in both directions. Expressing the first in the second and applying Corollary One gives r at most s. Expressing the second in the first gives s at most r. These two inequalities force r equals s.
We now introduce a maximal linearly independent subsystem.
Definition 13. A maximal linearly independent subsystem is an independent subsystem that becomes dependent whenever any other vector from the original system is added.

Maximal means that we cannot add another vector while keeping independence. A system containing a nonzero vector has such a subsystem: start with a nonzero vector and keep adding vectors whenever independence is preserved. The finite process must stop.
Result. Every maximal independent subsystem is equivalent to the full system.
Proof

Assume a maximal independent subsystem has been selected. We must express every vector of the original system in this subsystem. Its own members already have such expressions. For any other vector, maximality gives a dependence after it is added. The key is to show that the coefficient of the added vector cannot be zero.
Write a maximal independent subsystem as alpha sub one through alpha sub s. These vectors are already in the full system. For any remaining vector alpha sub j, adding it gives a dependence relation.
The coefficient ell cannot be zero. Otherwise, the independent subsystem would have a nonzero relation. Divide by ell to express alpha sub j in that subsystem.
Hence the full system can be expressed in the subsystem, and the subsystem in the full system. They are equivalent.
Theorem 3. All maximal independent subsystems of a given vector system contain the same number of vectors.
Proof
Each is equivalent to the full system, so any two are equivalent to each other. They are independent. Corollary Three of Theorem Two gives equal numbers of vectors.
The preceding theorem lets us define rank without depending on which maximal independent subsystem we choose.
Definition 14. The rank of a vector system is the number of vectors in a maximal independent subsystem. A system consisting entirely of zero vectors has rank zero.
Consequences. A system is independent exactly when its rank equals its number of vectors. Equivalent systems have the same rank.
Proof

An independent system is its own maximal independent subsystem. Conversely, if a maximal independent subsystem has as many vectors as the full system, it is the full system. For equivalent systems, their maximal independent subsystems are equivalent and independent, so their sizes agree. Systems of rank zero satisfy these statements directly.
rank 读 /ræŋk/，表示秩；maximal independent subsystem 极大线性无关组。按照原书约定，全零向量组的秩定为0。

title: Linear combinations of equations
zh: 方程的线性组合与同解

blocks.text: Result. Every solution of a system satisfies every linear combination of its equations. Systems whose augmented row vectors are equivalent have the same solutions.

The vector beta represents the equation with coefficients b sub one through b sub n and constant d. The equality says that this entire equation, including the constant, is a linear combination of the original equations.
Proof

Fix a solution of the original system. Our first goal is to show that it satisfies an arbitrary linear combination of the equations. For equivalent augmented row systems, we must then apply this observation in both directions to get equality of solution sets.

Multiply each original equation by its coefficient ell sub i and add. This proves that every original solution satisfies the new equation. For equivalent augmented row systems, apply this argument in both directions. Their solution sets are equal.

title: Row rank, column rank, and rank by minors
zh: 定义15—17 · 矩阵的秩

blocks.text: We first introduce row rank and column rank.
Definition 15. The row rank of a matrix is the rank of its row vectors. Its column rank is the rank of its column vectors.
Each row has n components. Each column has s components. These give two vector systems.
Next, we define minors of a rectangular matrix.
Definition 16. A minor of order k of a rectangular matrix is a determinant formed by selecting k rows and k columns, in their original order.
Min of s and n means the smaller of the two numbers. A minor is square even when the original matrix is rectangular.
We now define matrix rank using its nonzero minors.
Definition 17. The rank of a nonzero matrix is the largest order of a nonzero minor. The zero matrix has rank zero.

blocks.latex: \operatorname{rank}(A)=r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\begin{cases}\text{some minor of order }r\text{ is nonzero},\\\text{every minor of larger order is zero}\end{cases}\quad(r>0)

blocks.text: We read rank of A equals r. To check the second condition, it is enough to check order r plus one, if that order exists.
Result. If every minor of order r plus one is zero, all minors of larger order are zero.
Proof

We need to justify why vanishing minors of one order force vanishing at larger orders. Start with a minor of the next order and expand along one row. Every cofactor is a minor of the preceding order, so the assumption applies to each term. Repeat this argument for each larger order.
Expand any minor of order r plus two along one row. Every cofactor contains a minor of order r plus one, so the expansion is zero. Repeat for order r plus three, and continue. This proves the result.
rank(A) 是一个非负整数；不是行数，也不是非零元素数量。

title: Equality of row rank and column rank
zh: 定理4 · 行秩等于列秩

blocks.text: Theorem 4. The rank of a matrix equals its column rank and its row rank.
We follow the textbook proof using a nonzero minor. The zero matrix is immediate, so assume its rank r is positive.
Proof: independent columns

Let r be the largest order of a nonzero minor. To prove that the column rank is r, we need two facts: the columns selected by such a minor are independent, and every other column is their linear combination. We first prove independence, then construct the coefficients of those combinations. Finally we apply the same argument to the transpose for the row rank.

Reorder the columns so that a nonzero minor of order r lies in the first r columns. This does not change the column vectors as a system, or the largest order of a nonzero minor. Suppose the selected rows are i sub one through i sub r.
Cramer’s rule says the following homogeneous system has only the zero solution.
Thus the r columns restricted to these rows are independent. Adding their remaining components preserves independence. Therefore, the first r full columns of A are independent.
Proof: all other columns are combinations

Independence is now established. We must still prove that the same r columns express every remaining column, using coefficients that work in every row. Solving on the selected rows determines candidate coefficients; the vanishing larger minors will show that those candidates work on the other rows too.
Take another column j. Again by Cramer’s rule, choose ell sub one through ell sub r so the first r selected components satisfy the following equations.
For each row i, let b sub i one be the difference between its entry in column j and this linear combination. It is already zero on the selected rows.

For any other row i, form the minor with this row, the selected rows, column j, and the first r columns. It has order r plus one, so it is zero. Move row i and column j to the first positions; its value is still zero.
Subtract ell sub one times the second column, through ell sub r times the last column, from the first column. Now expand along that column.

Since d is nonzero, b sub i one is zero. Thus the same linear combination holds in every component. Every column is expressed in the first r independent columns. They form a maximal independent subsystem, so the column rank is r. If r already equals the number of columns, this last step is unnecessary.
Apply the same argument to the transpose. Corresponding minors have equal determinants, so the rank is unchanged, and its columns are the rows of A. Therefore, the row rank also equals r.
原书证明核心：先在非零子式的选定行上求系数，再用r+1阶子式为零把关系扩展到其余所有行。不能只证明局部关系就宣布整列相关。

title: Computing rank and choosing independent columns
zh: 定理4的推论1—4

blocks.text: Corollary 1. Elementary row and column operations preserve the rank, row rank, and column rank of a matrix.
Proof

An elementary operation has an inverse of the same kind. We will use this reversibility to show that the affected vector systems express each other. Then their ranks agree. The equality of matrix rank, row rank, and column rank transfers the conclusion to all three ranks.

After a column operation, the new columns are combinations of the old columns. The inverse operation expresses the old columns in the new ones. The column systems are equivalent, so their ranks agree. The rank equality theorem gives equality of all three ranks. Use rows for a row operation.
Corollary 2. The rank equals the number of nonzero rows in a row echelon form.
Proof

Choose the leading columns and the r nonzero rows. The displayed minor is upper triangular with nonzero diagonal entries. Every larger minor contains a zero row, so it is zero. Hence the echelon matrix has rank r. Row operations preserve rank, so the original matrix has rank r too.
Corollary 3. The columns of the original matrix at the leading-column positions of a row echelon form are a maximal independent subsystem of the original columns.
Proof

Take just these columns from the original and echelon matrices. The same row operations connect the two smaller matrices, so their ranks agree. The echelon columns have rank r by the displayed nonzero minor. Thus the selected original columns are independent. Their number is the rank of the full matrix, so they are maximal.
选的是原矩阵中对应位置的列，不是把变换后的列当作原向量。leading-column positions 主元列的位置。
Corollary 4. The rows or columns of a square matrix are dependent exactly when its determinant is zero, and independent exactly when its determinant is nonzero.
Proof

A square matrix has just one minor of order n: its determinant. It has rank n exactly when that determinant is nonzero. The rank equality theorem and the definition of vector independence give the conclusion.

title: Square systems: both directions
zh: 定理5—6 · 克拉默法则的逆命题

blocks.text: Theorem 5. A homogeneous system of n equations in n unknowns has a nonzero solution if and only if its coefficient determinant is zero.
Proof

For Theorem Five, the unknowns are coefficients of a linear combination of the columns of the coefficient matrix. A nonzero solution is therefore exactly a nontrivial dependence among those columns. This lets us connect the solution condition with the determinant condition in both directions.
A nonzero solution is a dependence relation among the columns of A. By the preceding corollary, the columns are dependent exactly when the determinant is zero. This proves both directions.
Theorem 6 (Cramer’s rule and its converse). A system of n equations in n unknowns has a unique solution if and only if its coefficient determinant is nonzero.
Proof

The nonzero-determinant direction is Cramer’s rule. Conversely, suppose c is the unique solution. If the associated homogeneous system had a nonzero solution d, adding the components would give another solution.
Since d is nonzero, this solution differs from c. That contradicts uniqueness. Thus the homogeneous system has only the zero solution. Theorem Five gives a nonzero determinant.

title: The consistency criterion
zh: 定理7 · 有解判别定理

blocks.text: Let us consider a linear system of s equations in n unknowns.
板书：完整写出方程组（1）。s equations in n unknowns：s 个方程、n 个未知量；a₁₁ 读 a sub one one。
Here, x one through x n are the unknowns. The coefficients and the constant terms belong to the number field P.
We can rewrite this system as a vector equation.
Let alpha sub j denote the column of coefficients of x sub j, and let beta denote the column of constant terms.
板书：按竖列写各向量，指向相应未知量的系数列。αⱼ 读 alpha sub j；xⱼ 读 x sub j；β 读 beta。
Each of these vectors has s components. The vectors alpha one through alpha n are the columns of the coefficient matrix.
Now system (1) becomes
读法：x sub one times alpha sub one, plus x sub two times alpha sub two, and so on, plus x sub n times alpha sub n, equals beta。
Comparing the components gives exactly the equations in system (1). So solving system (1) is the same as finding coefficients x one through x n that make this vector equation hold.
By the definition of a linear combination, we obtain the following equivalence.
System (1) has a solution if and only if beta is a linear combination of alpha one through alpha n.

blocks.latex: \text{System (1) has a solution}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\beta\text{ is a linear combination of }\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n.

blocks.text: How can we express this condition in terms of rank?
Let A denote the coefficient matrix, and let A bar denote the augmented matrix.
Here, the vectors inside the parentheses are the columns of the matrices. The augmented matrix is obtained by adding beta as the last column.
This leads to Theorem Seven.
Theorem 7. A linear system has a solution if and only if its coefficient matrix and its augmented matrix have the same rank.
读法：the rank of A equals the rank of A bar。consistent 表示有解，不表示唯一解。
Now, let us prove the theorem. We need to prove both directions.
Proof: necessity
necessity：必要性；从有解出发，证明两秩相等。
First, suppose that system (1) has a solution. We need to show that A and A bar have the same rank.
By the vector form of the system, beta is a linear combination of alpha one through alpha n.
Compare the following two vector systems:
Every vector in the second system is a linear combination of the first system: this is true for beta by our assumption, and for each alpha sub j because it already belongs to the first system.
Conversely, every vector in the first system belongs to the second system, so it is also a linear combination of that system.
Therefore, the two vector systems are equivalent. Equivalent vector systems have the same rank.
These are the column systems of A and A bar. Since the rank of a matrix equals the rank of its column system, we obtain
This proves necessity.
Proof: sufficiency
sufficiency：充分性；从两秩相等出发，证明有解。
Conversely, suppose that A and A bar have the same rank. Denote their common rank by r.
We need to show that system (1) has a solution. By the vector form, it is enough to show that beta is a linear combination of the columns of A.
First, if r equals zero, every entry of A bar is zero. In this case, setting all the unknowns equal to zero gives a solution.
Now suppose that r is greater than zero.
Choose a maximal linearly independent subsystem of the columns of A. It contains r vectors. After relabeling the columns, we may write it as
这里只是重新编号；若同时改写方程组，未知量也随对应列一起重新编号。
These vectors also belong to the column system of A bar, and they are still linearly independent.
The column system of A bar has rank r. Therefore, it cannot contain r plus one linearly independent vectors.
So the r vectors we have chosen also form a maximal linearly independent subsystem of
Every vector in this larger system is a linear combination of that maximal linearly independent subsystem. In particular, there exist scalars c one through c r such that
Since these vectors are columns of A, this also expresses beta as a linear combination of all the columns of A: we simply assign coefficient zero to every remaining column.
Thus, taking
板书：给前 r 个未知量取对应系数，其余取零。cⱼ 读 c sub j；分段条件读 for j from one through r / for j greater than r and at most n。
makes equation (2) hold. Therefore, system (1) has a solution.
This proves sufficiency and completes the proof.
Elimination form of the criterion. An inconsistent system has augmented rank exactly one greater than coefficient rank.
Justification

Adding one column can increase rank by at most one and cannot reduce it. By the theorem, unequal ranks mean no solution. In echelon form, the extra leading entry is in the constant column and gives an equation zero equals a nonzero number.

title: A general solution from a nonzero minor
zh: 用非零子式选自由未知量

blocks.text: We can also use Cramer’s rule to solve a general linear system. Let us see how.

For a consistent linear system of rank r in n unknowns, a nonzero minor of order r allows us to choose n minus r free unknowns. Once their values are fixed, the remaining r unknowns are uniquely determined.
Proof
Suppose that system (1) has a solution, and that
For now, assume that r is greater than zero. Choose a nonzero minor D of order r in A.
By reordering the equations and the unknowns, we may assume that D lies in the upper-left corner of A. In other words, it is formed from the first r rows and the first r columns.
板书：写出左上角非零子式；D 读 capital D；r 阶子式读 a minor of order r。

Since D is nonzero, its rows are linearly independent. Therefore, the first r rows of A bar are also linearly independent: any linear relation between these augmented rows would give the same relation between their first r components.
The rank of A bar is r, so these rows form a maximal linearly independent subsystem of its row system.
Thus, every remaining row of A bar is a linear combination of the first r rows.

Here, we are using the augmented rows, so the same linear combinations give both the coefficients and the constant terms. Therefore, every remaining equation is a linear combination of the first r equations.
Any solution of the first r equations satisfies all the remaining equations. Conversely, any solution of the original system certainly satisfies its first r equations.
So system (1) has exactly the same solutions as the following system.
板书：式（4）只保留前 r 个方程，仍保留 n 个未知量。
We now consider two cases.

If r equals n, system (4) has n equations in n unknowns, and its coefficient determinant is D, which is nonzero. By Cramer’s rule, it has a unique solution. Therefore, the original system also has a unique solution.
Now suppose that r is less than n.
In each equation, keep the terms involving x one through x r on the left. Move the terms involving x sub r plus one through x n to the right.
板书：移项得到式（5），改变项的位置，未删除未知量。
xᵣ₊₁ 读 x sub r plus one。第一行右边读：b sub one, minus a sub one comma r plus one times x sub r plus one, and so on, minus a sub one n times x sub n。
Choose any values in P for x sub r plus one through x n.
Once these values are fixed, the right-hand sides of (5) are fixed numbers. We can then regard (5) as a system of r equations in the r unknowns x one through x r.
Its coefficient determinant is still D, which is nonzero. By Cramer’s rule, these first r unknowns are uniquely determined.
So every choice of the last n minus r unknowns gives exactly one solution of the original system.
We call x sub r plus one through x n a set of free unknowns.
Applying Cramer’s rule to (5), we obtain expressions of the following form.
板书：式（6）表示前 r 个未知量如何由自由未知量确定。
The primed letters denote fixed coefficients obtained by solving the equations. They do not depend on the chosen values of the free unknowns.
d′₁ 读 d prime sub one；c′₁,ᵣ₊₁ 读 c prime sub one comma r plus one。prime 只作记号，不是求导。
Why do these expressions have this form?

In Cramer’s rule, each numerator is a determinant with one column replaced by the right-hand side of (5). That column is a fixed column plus a linear combination of columns with coefficients x sub r plus one through x n.
By linearity of the determinant in that column, each numerator has a constant term and terms linear in the free unknowns. Dividing by the fixed nonzero determinant D gives (6).
As the free unknowns range over P, formula (6) gives all solutions of system (1). This is the general solution.
Finally, if r equals zero, consistency implies that every entry of A bar is zero. Every equation is then zero equals zero, and all n unknowns can be chosen freely.

title: Sums and scalar multiples of solutions
zh: 齐次解的两条性质

blocks.text: We have found a condition for a linear system to have a solution. Next, we study the structure of its solutions.
Let us first consider the simpler case of a homogeneous linear system.
There are s equations in n unknowns. All coefficients belong to the number field P, and every right-hand side is zero. A solution is an ordered list of n values that satisfies every equation.
板书：完整写出齐次方程组（1）。后面本节的 system (1) 均指它。aᵢⱼ 读 a sub i j；x₁ through xₙ 读 x sub one through x sub n。
The set of its solutions has two important properties.
Property 1: addition
Assumption. The two vectors written below are solutions of system (1).
Conclusion. The sum of these two solution vectors is also a solution of system (1).
Proof
We must check that this sum satisfies every equation. For each row, substitute the sum and distribute the coefficients.
Thus the sum is a solution.
指向两组原解的等式，再指代入式。ℓ 读 lowercase ell，避免与数字 one 混淆。求和读 the sum from j equals one to n of a sub i j times k sub j。
Property 2: scalar multiplication
Assumptions. 1. The vector with components k sub one through k sub n is a solution of system (1).
2. The scalar c is any element of P.
Conclusion. Multiplying this solution vector by c gives another solution of system (1).
Proof
Substitute this scalar multiple into each equation. Take c outside the sum and use the fact that the original vector is a solution.
Thus every scalar multiple is a solution.
c 可以是零，也可以是任意非零数。c kⱼ 读 c times k sub j；不要把相乘读成下标。
Consequence. Every linear combination of solutions of a homogeneous linear system is again a solution of that system.
This follows by applying the two properties repeatedly. We now ask whether all solutions can be expressed using finitely many solution vectors.

title: A fundamental system of solutions
zh: 定义18 · 定理8及完整证明

blocks.text: We now define a fundamental system of solutions. It gives all solutions without keeping unnecessary vectors.
Definition 18. Let eta sub one through eta sub t be a system of solutions of the homogeneous system (1). If the following two conditions hold:
1. The solution vectors eta sub one through eta sub t are linearly independent;
2. Every solution of system (1) is a linear combination of these vectors;

blocks.latex: \text{for every solution }\eta,\ \text{there exist }k_1,\ldots,k_t\in P\text{ such that }\eta=k_1\eta_1+\cdots+k_t\eta_t;

blocks.text: then eta sub one through eta sub t is called a fundamental system of solutions of system (1).
按 If → 1、2 → then 的结构板书。η 读 eta；ηⱼ 是一个完整的 n 分量解向量，不是一个未知量。独立性中的零是零向量。
The second condition gives all solutions. The first prevents redundant vectors: if the vectors were dependent, one could be expressed using the others and removed.
We now prove that a fundamental system exists when the system has a nonzero solution.
Theorem 8
Consider a homogeneous linear system in n unknowns, with coefficient matrix A.
Assumptions
1. The system has a nonzero solution.
2. The rank of its coefficient matrix A is r.
Conclusions
1. The system has a fundamental system of solutions.
2. Every fundamental system of solutions contains exactly n minus r solution vectors.
nonzero solution：解向量的分量不全为零。n−r 是基础解系中向量的个数，不是说整个方程组只有 n−r 个解。
Proof: goals

We will construct n minus r solutions. Then we will check the two conditions in Definition Eighteen: independence and expression of every solution. Finally, we will prove that any other fundamental system has the same number of vectors.
The coefficient rank cannot be n. Otherwise, the homogeneous system would have only the zero solution. So r is less than n.
Step 1: construct the solution vectors
First suppose r is positive. As in the preceding section, reorder the equations and unknowns so that a nonzero minor of order r lies in the upper-left corner.
The first r equations have exactly the same solutions as the full system. Move the terms involving the last n minus r unknowns to the right.
