The last n minus r unknowns are free. Once their values are chosen, Cramer’s rule uniquely determines the first r unknowns. In particular, two solutions with the same free components must be equal.
板书：式（3）沿用§5的删去冗余方程和移项结果。强调“自由分量相同 → 完整解相同”，后面表示任意解时要用。
Choose the free components to be the following n minus r lists, one at a time.
Each choice gives exactly one solution. Denote these solutions by eta sub one through eta sub n minus r.
In each vector, the first r components are determined by the equations. The remaining components are the free values we chose.
指向前 r 个分量，再指向末尾的单位向量。cᵢⱼ 的第一个下标标记第几个解，第二个下标标记分量；cₙ₋ᵣ,₁ 读 c sub n minus r comma one。

If r is zero, every coefficient is zero and every vector in P to the n is a solution. In that case, choose the n unit vectors directly. There are no determined components, and the same checks below still apply.
Step 2: verify independence
Suppose a linear combination of the chosen solutions is the zero vector. We must show that every coefficient is zero.
Compare the last n minus r components. They are exactly the coefficients of the combination.
星号只表示暂时不需要计算的前 r 个分量，不是乘法；r=0 时没有这些分量。指最后 n−r 个位置逐一比较。
Thus the vectors are linearly independent. This verifies the first condition in the definition.
Step 3: express every solution
Let eta be any solution. Write out its components.
Use its free components as coefficients to form the following linear combination. Denote this new vector by zeta.
ζ 读 zeta。读法：zeta equals c sub r plus one times eta sub one, plus c sub r plus two times eta sub two, and so on, plus c sub n times eta sub n minus r。

Zeta is a solution by the two properties of homogeneous solutions. Its last n minus r components are the same as those of eta. The free components determine the full solution uniquely, so eta and zeta are equal.
This verifies the second condition. The chosen vectors form a fundamental system, so the first conclusion is proved.
Step 4: prove that the number is fixed

Let xi sub one through xi sub t be any other fundamental system. Each xi is a solution, so it is a linear combination of the eta vectors. Each eta is also a solution, so it is a linear combination of the xi vectors.
Thus the two vector systems are equivalent, and both are linearly independent. By the comparison result for independent vector systems, they contain the same number of vectors.
This proves the second conclusion and completes the proof.
ξ 读 xi；这里 ∼ 表示两个向量组等价，即可以互相线性表示。用前面向量组的比较结论，不提前使用维数定理。r=n 时只有零解，沿教材不引入空基础解系。
Consequence
Assumptions. 1. A vector system is equivalent to a fundamental system of solutions of (1).
2. The new vector system is linearly independent.
Conclusion. The new vector system is also a fundamental system of solutions of (1).
Proof

Every new vector is a linear combination of homogeneous solutions, so it is itself a solution. Every solution is a combination of the old system, and therefore of the new one. Together with the assumed independence, these facts give the definition.

title: The structure of all solutions
zh: 导出组 · 定理9及推论

blocks.text: We now return to a general linear system. We will relate its solutions to those of a homogeneous system.
Definition: the associated homogeneous system
Given a linear system over P, keep all its coefficients and replace every constant term by zero. The resulting system is called its associated homogeneous system, or derived system.
System (9) is the original system. System (1) is its associated homogeneous system. They have the same coefficient matrix. Only the constant terms change.
板书：先写原方程组（9），再指右端全部换成零得到（1）。associated homogeneous system 对应教材“导出组”；后面不要混淆两个系统的解。
There are two useful relations between their solutions.
Property 1: subtract two original solutions
Assumption. Two vectors are solutions of the same original system (9).
Conclusion. Their difference is a solution of the associated homogeneous system (1).
Proof
Subtract the two solution equalities in each row. The constant terms cancel.
So the difference satisfies every equation of the homogeneous system.
Property 2: add a homogeneous solution
Assumptions. 1. The vector gamma is a solution of the original system (9).
2. The vector eta is a solution of its associated homogeneous system (1).
Conclusion. The sum gamma plus eta is a solution of the original system (9).
Proof
Substitute the sum into each row. The original solution contributes the constant term, and the homogeneous solution contributes zero.
Thus the sum is an original solution.
γ 读 gamma；η 读 eta。性质1是“原解减原解 → 齐次解”；性质2是“原解加齐次解 → 原解”。
These two properties give Theorem Nine.
Theorem 9
Assumptions
1. The original linear system (9) is consistent.
2. Gamma sub zero is one fixed particular solution of (9), and (1) is its associated homogeneous system.
Conclusions
1. Every solution gamma of (9) can be written as gamma sub zero plus a solution eta of (1).
2. Every such sum is a solution of (9). Thus, as eta ranges over all solutions of (1), the formula gives all solutions of (9).
γ₀ 读 gamma sub zero；particular solution 特解。下标零只标记选定的特解，并不表示它是零向量。
Proof of conclusion 1
Let gamma be any solution of (9). Subtract the fixed solution gamma sub zero. By Property One, the difference is a homogeneous solution. Call it eta.
Proof of conclusion 2
Conversely, take any solution eta of (1). By Property Two, adding it to gamma sub zero gives a solution of (9). The two directions prove the theorem.
General solution using a fundamental system
Assumptions. 1. Gamma sub zero is a particular solution of (9).
2. The coefficient matrix has rank r less than n, and eta sub one through eta sub n minus r form a fundamental system of (1).
Conclusion. All solutions of (9), and only those solutions, are given by the following formula, with arbitrary coefficients in P.
By the definition of a fundamental system, the linear combination gives every homogeneous solution. Substitute it for eta in Theorem Nine.
读法：gamma equals gamma sub zero, plus k sub one times eta sub one, plus k sub two times eta sub two, and so on, plus k sub n minus r times eta sub n minus r。若 r=0，齐次部分可用 n 个单位向量；若 r=n，只剩特解，不引入空基础解系。
Corollary: uniqueness
Assumption. The original system (9) has at least one solution.
Conclusion. The solution of (9) is unique if and only if its associated homogeneous system (1) has only the zero solution.

blocks.latex: \text{(9) has a unique solution}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{(1) has only the zero solution.}

blocks.text: Proof: sufficiency

Suppose (1) has only the zero solution. If (9) had two different solutions, Property One would make their difference a nonzero solution of (1), a contradiction. Since (9) has a solution, that solution is unique.
Proof: necessity
Suppose (9) has a unique solution, gamma sub zero. If (1) had a nonzero solution eta, Property Two would give a different solution of (9).
This contradicts uniqueness. Therefore (1) has only the zero solution.
推论的“原方程组有解”不能省略。证明顺序沿教材：先充分性，再必要性。

title: A lemma on common polynomial factors
zh: §7引理 · 公因式与多项式恒等式

blocks.text: In the final section, we use linear systems to study two polynomial equations in two unknowns. First, we need a lemma about common factors.
Lemma: assumptions
1. The polynomials f and g are nonzero polynomials over the number field P, written with positive degree bounds n and m.
2. The leading displayed coefficients a sub zero and b sub zero are not both zero.
P[x] 读 P bracket x，表示 P 上的多项式。n、m 是写出的最高次数上界，未必都是实际次数；a₀、b₀ 至少一个非零。nonzero polynomial 指不恒等于零。
Lemma: conclusion
The polynomials f and g have a nonconstant common factor if and only if there exist nonzero polynomials u and v over P satisfying both of the following conditions:
1. The degree of u is less than m, and the degree of v is less than n.

blocks.latex: u,v\in P[x],\quad u\ne0,\quad v\ne0,\qquad\deg u<m,\quad\deg v<n

blocks.text: 2. The polynomial identity u times f equals v times g holds.
deg u < m 读 the degree of u is less than m。identity 表示多项式恒等式，不是只在某一个 x 值处相等。
Proof: necessity
Suppose f and g have a nonconstant common factor d. We must construct u and v with the required degrees and identity. Divide both polynomials by d.
Since f and g are nonzero, so are the two quotients. Their degrees are strictly below the displayed bounds.

blocks.latex: \deg f_1=\deg f-\deg d<n,\qquad\deg g_1=\deg g-\deg d<m

blocks.text: Set u equal to g sub one and v equal to f sub one. Then the required identity holds.
Proof: sufficiency
Conversely, suppose such nonzero u and v exist. We must find a nonconstant common factor of f and g.
Since the leading displayed coefficients are not both zero, we may exchange f and g if needed and assume a sub zero is nonzero. Thus f has degree n.
若交换 f、g，连同 n、m 以及 u、v 一起交换；交换后仍是同一个恒等式条件。
Let d be the greatest common divisor of f and v. Write both as d times their quotients.
Substitute into the identity and cancel the nonzero polynomial d.
Because d divides v, its degree is less than n. Since f has degree n, the quotient f sub one has positive degree.
The identity shows that f sub one divides v sub one times g. The two quotients are relatively prime, so the divisibility result from Chapter One implies that f sub one divides g.
It also divides f. Therefore f sub one is a nonconstant common factor of f and g, as required.
gcd 读 greatest common divisor；f₁∣g 读 f sub one divides g；此处竖线是整除。两个商互素和“互素因子整除乘积”的结论均来自第一章。

title: The resultant
zh: 结式定义 · 定理10及证明

blocks.text: We now turn the polynomial identity into a homogeneous linear system. Its unknowns will be the coefficients of u and v.
From a polynomial identity to linear equations
Use the same displayed forms of f and g as in the lemma. Write u and v with the required degree bounds.
The identity u times f equals v times g holds exactly when all corresponding coefficients are equal. Compare powers of x from m plus n minus one down to zero.
板书：这是按最高次到常数项展开的首尾示意；n 或 m 较小时，越界系数取零，重合的行只算一次。u₀ 读 u sub zero；a₁u₀ 读 a sub one times u sub zero。

For small values of n or m, some of the displayed rows coincide. The precise rule is one equation for each of the following m plus n coefficient positions. Coefficients outside their stated ranges are taken to be zero.
Move the right-hand sides to the left. We obtain m plus n homogeneous equations in the m plus n unknown coefficients listed below.
Let C denote their coefficient matrix, in this order of unknowns. The system has a nonzero solution if and only if the determinant of C is zero.
Transpose C, then change the signs of its last n rows. The resulting determinant is called the resultant.
Definition: the resultant
Given two polynomials f and g over P in the displayed forms above, with positive degree bounds n and m, construct an array as follows. The polynomials are allowed to be zero.
1. Its first m rows are the coefficient list of f, shifted one position to the right in each successive row.
2. Its last n rows are the coefficient list of g, shifted in the same way. All unused positions are zero.
The determinant of this array of order m plus n is called the resultant of f and g, denoted by R of f comma g.
这是移位阵的示意排布：上面共 m 行，每行放 n+1 个 f 的系数；下面共 n 行，每行放 m+1 个 g 的系数；每行总共 m+n 个位置。省略号按实际 n、m 展开，不把示意图的可见行数当作阶数。
We read R of f comma g, or the resultant of f and g. Transposition preserves a determinant, and each row sign change multiplies it by minus one. Therefore the two determinants vanish together.
We can now state the exact criterion, including the case where displayed leading coefficients vanish.
Theorem 10: assumptions
1. The polynomials f and g belong to P bracket x and are written in the displayed forms. Either or both polynomials may be zero.
2. The displayed degree bounds n and m are positive. The leading displayed coefficients are a sub zero and b sub zero.
Theorem 10: conclusion
The resultant R of f and g is zero if and only if at least one of the following alternatives holds:
Either f and g have a nonconstant common factor in P bracket x,
or both leading displayed coefficients a sub zero and b sub zero are zero.
这里是“或”，不是同时满足两项；两种情形也可能同时出现。“最高显示系数”可为零，不能直接当作实际最高次项系数。
Proof: from either alternative to a zero resultant
First, if both leading displayed coefficients are zero, the first column of the resultant array is zero. So the resultant is zero.
Now suppose the polynomials have a nonconstant common factor. If one polynomial is zero, its whole group of rows is zero, and the resultant is zero.

If both polynomials are nonzero and the leading displayed coefficients are not both zero, the lemma gives nonzero u and v with the required degree bounds and with u times f equal to v times g. Their coefficients give a nonzero solution of the homogeneous system. Hence its determinant, and therefore the resultant, is zero.

blocks.latex: uf=vg,\quad u,v\ne0,\quad\deg u<m,\quad\deg v<n\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\det C=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad R(f,g)=0

blocks.text: Proof: from a zero resultant to either alternative
Conversely, suppose the resultant is zero. We must prove that at least one of the stated alternatives holds.
Case 1: both leading displayed coefficients vanish
If a sub zero and b sub zero are both zero, the second alternative already holds.
Case 2: at least one polynomial is zero
If both polynomials are zero, any polynomial of positive degree divides both. If exactly one is zero and the other has positive degree, the other polynomial is itself a nonconstant common factor.

If exactly one is zero and the other is a nonzero constant, both leading displayed coefficients are zero, because n and m are positive. Thus one of the alternatives holds in every zero-polynomial case.
Case 3: neither polynomial is zero
It remains to consider nonzero f and g with leading displayed coefficients not both zero. The zero resultant gives a nonzero solution of the homogeneous coefficient system.

Use these coefficients to form u and v. They satisfy u times f equals v times g and are not both zero. Since f and g are nonzero, if either u or v were zero, the identity would force the other to be zero as well. Thus both are nonzero.
All assumptions of the lemma now hold. It gives a nonconstant common factor of f and g. This completes the proof.
Consequence over the complex numbers
Under the assumptions of Theorem 10, with P equal to the complex field, the resultant is zero if and only if the polynomials have a common complex root or both leading displayed coefficients vanish.
Justification
A common root gives the common factor x minus that root. Conversely, a nonconstant common factor over the complex numbers has a root, and that root belongs to both polynomials.
common root 公共根；nonconstant common factor 非常数公因式。复数域中的根的结论是下一知识点的依据。

title: Eliminating one variable
zh: 定理11 · 二元高次方程组

blocks.text: We now use the resultant to eliminate one variable from two polynomial equations over the complex numbers.
Set-up
1. The polynomials f and g are polynomials in x and y with complex coefficients. We seek all pairs of complex numbers that satisfy both equations.
2. Regard f and g as polynomials in x, with coefficients that are polynomials in y. Use positive displayed degree bounds n and m.

blocks.latex: a_i(y),b_j(y)\in\mathbb C[y]\qquad(0\le i\le n,\ 0\le j\le m)

blocks.text: bivariate 二元；ℂ[y] 读 polynomials in y over the complex numbers。固定 y 后得到的是关于 x 的一元多项式，实际次数可能降低，也可能变为零多项式。
The resultant that eliminates x
Form the resultant array using these coefficient polynomials in y. Its determinant, denoted by R sub x of f comma g, is a polynomial in y.
The top group has m rows, and the bottom group has n rows. The subscript x tells us which variable is eliminated. The resulting polynomial involves only y.
板书：结式阵仍为 m+n 阶，省略号按实际尺寸延伸。Rₓ(f,g) 读 R sub x of f comma g；Rₓ(f,g)(y₀) 读 the resultant evaluated at y sub zero。
Theorem Eleven gives both the necessary condition and the precise converse.
Theorem 11: from a solution to a resultant root
Assumption. The pair (x sub zero, y sub zero) is a complex solution of both equations in (8).
Conclusion. The number y sub zero is a root of R sub x of f comma g.
Theorem 11: converse
Assumption. The complex number y sub zero is a root of R sub x of f comma g.
Conclusion. At least one of the following alternatives holds:
Either both leading displayed coefficients vanish at y sub zero,
or there exists a complex number x sub zero such that the pair (x sub zero, y sub zero) solves both original equations.
两个结论用 either ... or ... 连接，不能读成同时成立。结式的根只是候选 y 值；最高显示系数同时为零时，未必存在对应的 x。
Proof: fix y and compare resultants

Fix y equal to y sub zero. Substitution commutes with addition and multiplication in a determinant. Thus evaluating the resultant at this y value gives the resultant of the two resulting polynomials in x.
右边仍使用原来的显示次数上界 n、m 构造结式；不能因代入后次数降低，就擅自换成较小的结式阵。
Proof: forward direction

Suppose the pair is a common solution. Then x minus x sub zero divides both polynomials obtained by fixing y. By Theorem Ten, their resultant is zero. The displayed identity proves the first conclusion.
Proof: converse

Suppose y sub zero is a root of the resultant. Apply Theorem Ten to the two polynomials obtained by fixing y. Either both leading displayed coefficients are zero, or the polynomials have a nonconstant common factor.

The first possibility is exactly the first alternative. In the second possibility, a nonconstant polynomial over the complex numbers has a complex root. Let x sub zero be such a root. Since the factor divides both polynomials, this value solves both original equations.

blocks.latex: d(x)\mid f(x,y_0),\quad d(x)\mid g(x,y_0),\quad\deg d>0,\quad d(x_0)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(x_0,y_0)=g(x_0,y_0)=0

blocks.text: This gives the second alternative and proves the theorem.
Elimination procedure
Assumption. The resultant R sub x of f comma g is not the zero polynomial.
Step 1. Find all complex roots of the resultant, regarded as a polynomial in y. These are the only possible y coordinates of solutions.
Step 2. Substitute each candidate y value into both original equations and find all their common roots in x.
Step 3. Keep precisely the pairs that satisfy both original equations. Together, they are all solutions of the original system.

The forward direction ensures that no solution is missed. Substitution rejects candidates that do not give a common solution, including possible cases where both leading displayed coefficients vanish.
Special cases
If the resultant is a nonzero constant, it has no roots, so the original system has no solutions.
For a candidate y value, if both resulting polynomials in x are zero, every complex x is allowed. If just one is zero, use all roots of the other. A nonzero constant equation gives no solution.
If the resultant is identically zero, the finite list of candidate y values in Step 1 is unavailable. This procedure does not by itself determine all solutions.
In that case we must examine the original polynomials further, for example by factoring them or trying to eliminate the other variable. The original equations must still be satisfied.
eliminate x 消去 x；identically zero 恒等于零。结式非零只保证候选 y 值有限，并不排除某个候选值对应所有 x。

title: Matrix notation and equality
zh: 矩阵的记号与相等

blocks.text: We begin matrix operations by fixing their objects and the meaning of equality. Before comparing entries, check that both matrices have the same numbers of rows and columns. Only then can the phrase corresponding entries be used.
We now begin the chapter on matrices. First, let us state the notation and the rule for equality.
A matrix with s rows and n columns is an s by n matrix. Two matrices are equal if they have the same size and all corresponding entries are equal.

blocks.latex: A=B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a_{ij}=b_{ij}\quad(1\le i\le s,\ 1\le j\le n),\qquad A,B\text{ of size }s\times n.

blocks.text: We denote the matrix by capital A. The entry a sub i j is in row i and column j. Read s times n as “s by n.” To prove two matrices equal, we will compare their sizes and their entries.
A row vector is a one by n matrix. A column vector is an n by one matrix.
Read the entries as “a sub one, a sub two, through a sub n.” From now on, all entries belong to the number field P.
先写矩阵及尺寸，再说明相等的两个条件。矩阵用圆括号；竖线表示方阵的行列式。P读作“the number field P”。

title: Addition and subtraction
zh: 定义1：加法、零矩阵与负矩阵

blocks.text: First, let us define matrix addition.
We first define addition for matrices of the same size.
Definition 1. The sum of two matrices of the same size is obtained by adding corresponding entries.
The entry in row i and column j is a sub i j plus b sub i j. The two matrices must have the same number of rows and columns.
Matrix addition is associative and commutative.
Proof

Assume the matrices have the same size. To prove either addition law, compare an arbitrary entry on its two sides. The entries are scalars in P, so their sums satisfy commutativity and associativity. Equality at every position gives equality of the matrices.
Compare the entries in row i and column j. These equalities follow from addition in P.
The zero matrix has all entries zero. The negative of A has entries −aᵢⱼ. Subtraction is defined by adding the negative matrix.
We denote the zero matrix by capital O. Read minus A as “the negative of A.” The last two identities hold because each entry satisfies a plus zero equals a, and a plus negative a equals zero.

title: Rank of a sum
zh: 矩阵和的秩

blocks.text: We next state a consequence of matrix addition.
For matrices A and B of the same size, the rank of A plus B is at most the sum of their ranks.
Read this as “the rank of A plus B is less than or equal to the rank of A plus the rank of B.”
Proof

Assume A and B have the same size. Each row of A plus B is the sum of one row of A and one row of B. We will express all these rows using a maximal independent subsystem of each original row system, giving at most the sum of the two ranks as a bound.
Let alpha sub i and beta sub i be row i of A and B. Row i of A plus B is their sum.

Choose a maximal linearly independent set of rows from A, and one from B. Let their sizes be r and t. Every row of A plus B is a linear combination of these r plus t vectors. Its row rank is therefore at most r plus t. This proves the inequality.
原书仅指出由向量组的秩得出。这里展开这一推理；alpha、beta只是明确写出的行向量，不替代定义中的矩阵板书。

title: Matrix multiplication
zh: 定义2：矩阵乘法

blocks.text: Next, let us define matrix multiplication.
We now define matrix multiplication. The number of columns of the first factor must equal the number of rows of the second.
Definition 2. If A is s by n and B is n by m, their product AB is the s by m matrix whose entry cᵢⱼ is the sum of the products of corresponding entries in row i of A and column j of B.

blocks.latex: A=(a_{ik})_{s\times n},\quad B=(b_{kj})_{n\times m},\quad C=AB=(c_{ij})_{s\times m}.

blocks.text: The number of columns of A must equal the number of rows of B. The product has s rows and m columns. To find c sub i j, take row i of A and column j of B. Multiply corresponding entries, then add the products.

Read the sum as “the sum from k equals one to n of a sub i k times b sub k j.” In the expanded form, say “a sub i one times b sub one j, plus a sub i two times b sub two j, and so on, up to a sub i n times b sub n j.”
板书先标尺寸，再写元素公式；用手指明A的第i行和B的第j列。乘法不是对应元素直接相乘。

title: Associativity of multiplication
zh: 矩阵乘法结合律及证明

blocks.text: Now let us prove the associative law.
Matrix multiplication is associative whenever the products are defined.

blocks.latex: A=(a_{ij})_{s\times n},\quad B=(b_{jk})_{n\times m},\quad C=(c_{kl})_{m\times r},\qquad(AB)C=A(BC).

blocks.text: Proof

Assume the sizes of A, B, and C allow both products. We must show that AB times C and A times BC have the same entry in every row and column. Expand one entry using the product definition twice, then reorder the finite scalar sums.
Following the textbook, denote AB by V and BC by W. Write their entries first.

blocks.latex: V=AB=(v_{ik})_{s\times m},\quad v_{ik}=\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_{ij}b_{jk};\qquad W=BC=(w_{jl})_{n\times r},\quad w_{jl}=\sum_{k=1}^{m}b_{jk}c_{kl}.

blocks.text: Both products in the statement are s by r. In row i and column l, the entry of V C is the following sum.
In the same position, the entry of A W is as follows.
These finite double sums contain exactly the same terms. Only the order of summation changes. Thus every pair of corresponding entries is equal. This proves the result.
l是小写字母ell。双重求和读“the sum over k from one to m, and over j from one to n”。两边乘积尺寸相同也是矩阵相等的条件。

title: Order matters in multiplication
zh: 乘法不交换与消去律失效

blocks.text: We now examine which familiar scalar rules fail for matrices. In each example, check that the products exist and calculate both sides. A single example where the proposed rule fails is enough to show that it is not a general matrix law.
The associative law holds, but we must keep the order of the factors.
Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general. A product of two nonzero matrices can be zero. Cancellation does not hold in general.
Verification
Here A B is zero, but B A is not zero. Thus they are different. Also, both A and B are nonzero. Finally, A B equals A O, but B is not O. So we cannot cancel A.
There is also a size issue. Even when A B is defined, B A may not be defined. When both are defined, they may have different sizes.
保留原书这个反例，因为它直接证明三条重要结论；不加入一般计算练习。

title: Identity and distributive laws
zh: 定义3：单位矩阵与分配律

blocks.text: We now introduce the identity matrix.
We now introduce the identity matrix.
Definition 3. The identity matrix Eₙ has ones on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

blocks.latex: E_n=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&\cdots&0\\0&1&\cdots&0\\\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\0&0&\cdots&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad A_{s\times n}E_n=A_{s\times n},\quad E_sA_{s\times n}=A_{s\times n}.

blocks.text: We denote this matrix by E sub n. In A E sub n, column j of E has just one nonzero entry. It selects a sub i j from row i of A. The same argument applies to E sub s times A. Thus both products equal A.
Matrix multiplication satisfies both distributive laws, whenever the sizes match.
Proof

To justify the identity and distributive laws, keep the matrix sizes compatible at every step. Compare an arbitrary entry on each side. The identity matrix selects a single entry, while distributivity follows by splitting a scalar sum inside the entry formula.
For the first identity, compare the entries in row i and column j. Let n be the number of columns of A.
For the second identity, let n be the number of columns of B and C. Again, compare the entries.
These are the distributive laws for numbers. They prove both matrix identities. We need both laws because we cannot change the order of matrix factors.

title: Powers of a square matrix
zh: 方阵的幂与运算法则

blocks.text: Next, we define positive integer powers of a square matrix.
For a square matrix A, define A¹ = A and Aᵏ⁺¹ = AᵏA. Thus Aᵏ is the product of k copies of A.
Read A to the power k, or simply A to the k. This definition requires A to be square, so that repeated multiplication is possible.
For positive integers k and l, powers of the same matrix satisfy the following laws.
Proof

All factors here are copies of the same square matrix. Associativity lets us regroup them without changing their order. Count the number of factors to justify the product and power laws; no commutation of different matrices is being assumed.

In the first product, there are k copies of A followed by l copies. By associativity, we can remove the brackets. There are k plus l copies in total. In the second product, there are l groups, each containing k copies of A. There are k l copies in total. Associativity gives the second identity.
These laws concern powers of the same matrix. For different matrices A and B, the k-th power of A B need not equal A to the k times B to the k, because changing the order of factors is not allowed.

title: Scalar multiplication
zh: 定义4：数量乘法及运算律

blocks.text: We next define multiplication by a scalar. Here a scalar means a number in P.
We first define scalar multiplication of a matrix.
Definition 4. The scalar multiple kA is obtained by multiplying every entry of A by k.
Scalar multiplication satisfies the following laws, for compatible matrices and scalars k and l.
Proof

The scalars lie in P and all matrix sums and products have compatible sizes. For the stated laws, compare corresponding entries and move only scalar factors through the finite sums. This reduces each identity to a law in P.

The first four laws follow entry by entry from the corresponding laws for numbers. For example, k times the sum of a sub i j and b sub i j equals k a sub i j plus k b sub i j. Let us prove the last law as in the textbook. Let A be s by n and B be n by m. Compare their entries in position i, t.
All three entries are equal. This proves the identity.
A scalar matrix is a matrix kE. It commutes with every square matrix of the same order.
This follows from the last scalar multiplication law and the identity matrix rule. The scalar matrix rules below follow in the same way.

title: Transpose and its laws
zh: 定义5：转置及乘积转置的证明

blocks.text: Next, we define the transpose of a matrix.
We now define the transpose of a matrix.
Definition 5. The transpose Aᵀ is obtained by interchanging the rows and columns of A. An s by n matrix becomes an n by s matrix.
Read A superscript T as “A transpose.” Row i of A becomes column i of A transpose. The superscript T is a transpose symbol, not a numerical power.
Transposition satisfies the following four identities. In the transpose of a product, the order of the factors is reversed.

blocks.latex: (A^{\mathrm T})^{\mathrm T}=A,\quad(A+B)^{\mathrm T}=A^{\mathrm T}+B^{\mathrm T},\quad(AB)^{\mathrm T}=B^{\mathrm T}A^{\mathrm T},\quad(kA)^{\mathrm T}=kA^{\mathrm T}.

blocks.text: Proof

For the product identity, suppose A is s by n and B is n by m. Both the transpose of AB and B transpose times A transpose have size m by s. We must compare their i j entries, taking care that transposition interchanges the entry indices and reverses the factor order.

Transposing twice restores every entry. Addition and scalar multiplication act on each entry, so they also commute with transposition. We now prove the product formula. Let A be s by n and B be n by m. Both sides are m by s. First, the entry in position i, j of A B is the following sum.

Here the subscript i j on a matrix expression means its entry in row i and column j. After transposing, we use the original entry in row j and column i. Now compare this with B transpose times A transpose.
The entries agree. This proves the formula. In the last step we exchanged two numbers inside each term. We did not exchange the matrix factors.

title: Determinants of matrix products
zh: 定理1及推论1：乘积的行列式

blocks.text: We now study the determinant and rank of a product.
Theorem 1. For two n by n matrices A and B over P, the determinant of AB equals the product of their determinants.
The vertical bars mean the determinant. Read this as “the determinant of A B equals the determinant of A times the determinant of B.”
Proof

Assume A and B are square matrices of the same order n. Our goal is the determinant identity. We will match the entry formula for AB with the determinant multiplication rule already proved in Chapter Two. This checks the hypotheses and the exact matrix to which that earlier rule applies.

The entry in row i and column j of A B is the sum from k equals one to n of a sub i k times b sub k j. The multiplication rule proved in Chapter Two, Section Eight, applies to exactly this determinant. It gives the stated equality.
原书直接引用第二章§8的乘法规则；该完整证明已保留在前文“determinant-product”，此处按原书不重复展开。
Corollary 1. The determinant of a product of any finite number of square matrices of the same order equals the product of their determinants.
Proof

Use induction on m. The case m equals two is Theorem One. Assume the formula holds for m minus one factors. Apply Theorem One to the first m minus one factors and the last factor. Then use the induction hypothesis.

title: Singular and nonsingular matrices
zh: 定义6及推论2：退化与非退化矩阵

blocks.text: We next introduce two terms for square matrices.
We first introduce the terms singular and nonsingular for square matrices.
Definition 6. A square matrix A is nonsingular if its determinant is nonzero. It is singular if its determinant is zero.
Here A has order n. Nonsingular means non-degenerate; singular means degenerate. The rank criterion follows from the relation between rank and nonzero minors in Chapter Three.
Corollary 2. For square matrices A and B of the same order, AB is singular if and only if at least one of A and B is singular.
Proof

Assume A and B are square matrices of the same order. Their product is singular precisely when its determinant is zero. The determinant product formula turns this into a product of two scalars, which is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero.

By Theorem One, the determinant of A B is the product of two numbers, the determinants of A and B. A product of two numbers in P is zero if and only if at least one factor is zero. This proves both directions.
“if and only if”表示充要条件。此处对数域中的两个数使用零乘积性质，不能直接对两个矩阵使用这一性质。

title: Rank of a matrix product
zh: 定理2及推论：矩阵乘积的秩

blocks.text: Finally, let us prove the rank inequality for a product.
Theorem 2. If A is n by m and B is m by s, then the rank of AB is at most the rank of each factor.
Read min as “the minimum of.” We will prove two inequalities, one for each factor.
Proof

We need two inequalities. First express each column of AB in the columns of A to bound its column rank. Then express each row of AB in the rows of B to obtain the other bound. Use equality of row and column rank to state both as inequalities of matrix ranks.

As in the textbook, let B sub one through B sub m be the rows of B. Let C sub one through C sub n be the rows of A B. These capital letters now denote row vectors. From the multiplication rule, we obtain the following expression for row i.
To check this equality, compare component j. On both sides, it is the sum from k equals one to m of a sub i k times b sub k j.

Thus every row of A B is a linear combination of the rows of B. Choose a maximal independent set of rows of B. These rows also express every row of A B. Hence A B cannot have more independent rows than B.
Now use columns. Let A sub one through A sub m be the columns of A. Let D sub one through D sub s be the columns of A B.
Each column of A B is a linear combination of the columns of A. The same rank argument gives the other inequality.
Combining the two inequalities proves the theorem.
Corollary. The rank of a product of several compatible matrices is at most the rank of any factor.
Proof

Apply Theorem Two repeatedly. The rank of the full product is at most the rank of the product of the first t minus one factors, and at most the rank of the last factor. By induction, it is at most the rank of every factor.
这里行向量Bᵢ、Cᵢ和列向量Aᵢ、Dᵢ均沿用原书；先展示完整矩阵再引入，切勿混淆A（矩阵）和Aᵢ（第i列）。

title: The inverse of a matrix
zh: 定义7—8：可逆矩阵与逆的唯一性

blocks.text: We now study matrix inverses. Throughout this section, A is a square matrix of order n, and E is the identity matrix of order n.
We now define invertibility of a square matrix. Both product identities are part of the definition.
Definition 7. A matrix A is invertible if there is a matrix B of the same order such that AB = BA = E.
We require both products to be the identity. First, let us show that such a matrix B is unique.
If a matrix has an inverse, that inverse is unique.
Proof

For uniqueness, assume B and C both satisfy the two inverse identities for the same square matrix A. Our goal is B equals C. Insert the identity AC next to B, and use associativity and BA equals E to reach C.
Start with B sub one. Replace E by A B sub two. Use associativity to group B sub one with A. Their product is E. We are left with B sub two. This proves uniqueness.
Having proved uniqueness, we can name this matrix the inverse and introduce its notation.
Definition 8. The matrix B satisfying AB = BA = E is called the inverse of A, denoted by A⁻¹.
Read A to the minus one as “A inverse.” It denotes a matrix, not the reciprocal of each entry.
先写可逆定义的两个等式，再证明唯一性，最后引入A⁻¹。唯一性证明只用结合律，不交换矩阵的先后次序。

title: The adjugate matrix
zh: 定义9：伴随矩阵及基本恒等式

blocks.text: Next, we define the adjugate matrix. This will give us a formula for the inverse.
We now introduce the adjugate matrix. Its construction uses the cofactors, with their indices transposed.
Definition 9. The adjugate of A is the transpose of the matrix of its cofactors. It is denoted by A*.

Capital A sub i j is the cofactor of the entry small a sub i j. M sub i j is its minor. Notice the positions: capital A sub i j goes into row j and column i of A star. Read A star as “the adjugate of A.”
If d is the determinant of A, then AA* = A*A = dE.
Proof

To prove the displayed matrix identities, compare their diagonal and off-diagonal entries. A diagonal entry is a cofactor expansion of the determinant of A. An off-diagonal entry is the corresponding expansion with a repeated row or column, so it is zero.

In A A star, the entry in row i and column j is the following sum. If i equals j, it is the expansion of the determinant along row i. If i is different from j, the sum is zero by the cofactor identity from Chapter Two.
For A star A, use the same identity for columns.
Thus both products have d on the diagonal and zero elsewhere. This proves the identity, even when d is zero.
星号沿用原书表示伴随矩阵，不表示共轭转置。先指明余子式的转置位置，再写两种乘积的元素；cases读“d if i equals j, and zero otherwise”。

title: When is a matrix invertible?
zh: 定理3：可逆条件与求逆公式

blocks.text: We can now state the main criterion for invertibility.
Theorem 3. A square matrix is invertible if and only if it is nonsingular. When d = |A| is nonzero, its inverse is A* divided by d.
Read the formula as “A inverse equals one over d times A star.” We divide every entry of the adjugate by the determinant.
Proof

We must prove both directions. First assume the determinant is nonzero. Divide the adjugate by this scalar and verify the two inverse identities to prove sufficiency. Then assume an inverse exists. Taking determinants of an inverse identity shows that the determinant of A cannot vanish, proving necessity.
First, suppose d is nonzero. From the adjugate identity, we get both of the required products.
Thus A is invertible, and the displayed matrix is its inverse. Conversely, suppose A is invertible. Take determinants in A A inverse equals E.
Since this product is one, the determinant of A cannot be zero. Hence A is nonsingular. This proves both directions.

title: A one-sided inverse is enough for square matrices
zh: 方阵的单侧逆与逆矩阵的行列式

blocks.text: The definition uses two equalities. For square matrices of the same order, one of them is enough, as a consequence of Theorem Three.
If A and B are square matrices of the same order and AB = E, then both are invertible and B = A⁻¹.
Proof

Assume A and B are square of the same order and AB equals E. We cannot cancel A before proving it invertible. Instead, take determinants to show that both determinants are nonzero, apply the invertibility criterion, and only then multiply by the inverse.
Take determinants. Their product is one, so neither determinant is zero. By Theorem Three, both matrices are invertible. Multiply A B equals E on the left by A inverse.
It follows that B A equals E as well. The condition that both matrices are square is essential here.
The determinant of an inverse is the reciprocal of the original determinant.
Proof

We already know that the determinant of A times the determinant of A inverse is one. Divide by the nonzero number d. Read the result as “the determinant of A inverse equals one over the determinant of A.”

title: Inverses of transposes and products
zh: 推论：转置与乘积的逆

blocks.text: Next, let us state two rules for inverses.
Corollary. If A and B are invertible matrices of the same order, then Aᵀ and AB are invertible, and the following formulas hold.

Read the first formula as “the inverse of A transpose equals the transpose of A inverse.” Read the second as “the inverse of A B equals B inverse times A inverse.” Notice the reversed order in the second formula.
Proof

The assumptions give two-sided inverses for A and B. To establish a proposed inverse formula, multiply the proposed matrix by the original matrix in both orders and obtain E. For a product, keep the order of the factors exactly as written.

The determinants of A transpose and A B are nonzero, by the determinant rules. So both are invertible. To identify the first inverse, transpose both equalities in A A inverse equals A inverse A equals E.
Thus the transpose of A inverse is the inverse of A transpose. For the product formula, check both products directly.
These equalities use associativity. The inverse factors cancel in the middle because their order is reversed. By the definition of the inverse, the second formula follows.

title: Solving a linear system with an inverse
zh: 用逆矩阵推导克拉默法则

blocks.text: We can now give the textbook's matrix proof of the solution formula for a nonsingular linear system.
If A is nonsingular, the system AX = B has the unique solution X = A⁻¹B. Its entries are given by Cramer's rule.
Proof

Assume A is nonsingular. We must prove existence and uniqueness separately. First substitute A inverse B into AX equals B to obtain a solution. Then start with an arbitrary solution and multiply on the left by A inverse; this forces every solution to be that same vector.
First, substitute A inverse B into the system. This proves existence.
Next, let C be any solution column. Then A C equals B. Multiply on the left by A inverse. This proves uniqueness.
To recover Cramer's rule, look at row j of the adjugate times B. Let D sub j be the determinant obtained by replacing column j of A with B.
Expanding D sub j along column j gives the numerator. Its cofactors are unchanged because deleting the replaced column leaves the same minors. This gives Cramer's formula.
B在这里是常数项列向量，C是任意解列向量，不是上一小节的方阵。A⁻¹B读“A inverse times B”。

title: Invertible multiplication preserves rank
zh: 定理4：可逆乘法不改变秩

blocks.text: We finish this section with a rank theorem.
Theorem 4. Let A be s by n. If P is an invertible s by s matrix and Q is an invertible n by n matrix, then multiplying A by P on the left or by Q on the right does not change its rank.
Here capital P denotes a matrix. In this statement it does not denote the number field. We will prove each equality using two opposite inequalities.
Proof

The product-rank inequality first gives that multiplying A cannot increase its rank. To obtain the reverse inequality, recover A by multiplying the new product by the inverse of P or Q. The two inequalities together give equality.
Put B equals P A. By Theorem Two, the rank of B is at most the rank of A. Since P is invertible, we can also write A as P inverse B.
Combining the inequalities gives equality. For multiplication on the right, write C equals A Q and A equals C Q inverse. Apply Theorem Two again.
Therefore the ranks of A and A Q are also equal. This completes the proof.

title: Block matrices and multiplication
zh: 矩阵分块与分块乘法公式

blocks.text: We now turn to block matrices. We divide a matrix into smaller rectangular matrices by cutting between rows and between columns. These smaller matrices are called blocks.
Block multiplication follows the usual row-by-column rule, provided the column partition of A matches the row partition of B.

Capital A sub p k is a whole block, of size s sub p by n sub k. It is not a single entry. The matching block B sub k q has n sub k rows. Thus each product has size s sub p by m sub q. Read the formula as “C sub p q equals the sum from k equals one to ell of A sub p k times B sub k q.”
Proof

The column widths of the first block matrix must match the row heights of the second. For each output block, the usual entry formula splits its summation index into those shared ranges. This produces the block row-by-column formula, with the order of every product preserved.

In the ordinary multiplication formula, each entry of A B is a sum over all columns of A. Split this sum into the l consecutive groups specified by the partition. Group k is exactly the corresponding entry of the block product A sub p k times B sub k q. Adding all groups gives the displayed formula. This holds for every entry of every block.
For two block rows and two block columns, write the rule in full.
小写l读ell；sₚ、nₖ、m_q分别是分块尺寸。关键是每一道分割线都对应，只有总列数等于总行数还不够。保持每个块乘积的先后次序。

title: Inverse of a block triangular matrix
zh: 分块三角矩阵的求逆推导

blocks.text: Next, we use block multiplication to find an inverse. This is the block inverse formula derived in the textbook.
If A and B are invertible square matrices of orders k and r, and C is r by k, then the following block triangular matrix D is invertible, with the displayed inverse.
The upper right O is the k by r zero matrix. Read the lower left block of the inverse as “minus B inverse times C times A inverse.”
Proof

Assume both diagonal blocks are invertible and C has the stated size. The target is to verify that the proposed block matrix is a two-sided inverse. Multiply in both orders: the diagonal blocks become identities, and the off-diagonal terms must cancel.
First, the block triangular determinant formula gives the determinant of D. Since both diagonal blocks are invertible, this determinant is nonzero.
Therefore D has an inverse. Write its four unknown blocks as X sub one one, X sub one two, X sub two one, and X sub two two. Multiply D by this inverse.
Compare the four blocks on both sides. We get four matrix equations.
The first two equations give X sub one one equals A inverse, and X sub one two equals zero. Substitute the zero block into the fourth equation. It gives X sub two two equals B inverse.
Finally, use the third equation. Move C X sub one one to the other side, substitute A inverse, and multiply on the left by B inverse.
These are exactly the four blocks in the stated formula. The order of the three factors in the lower left block must be kept.

title: Diagonal and block diagonal matrices
zh: 对角矩阵、准对角矩阵及运算

blocks.text: We finish with diagonal and block diagonal matrices.
A diagonal matrix has zero entries outside the main diagonal. A block diagonal matrix has square blocks on the main diagonal and zero blocks elsewhere.

Each small a sub i is a number. Each capital A sub i is a square matrix of order n sub i. The orders of different diagonal blocks may differ. A diagonal matrix is the special case in which every block has order one.
Two block diagonal matrices with matching block sizes can be added and multiplied block by block. If each diagonal block is invertible, the inverse is obtained by inverting each diagonal block.
Proof

The zero off-diagonal blocks make each diagonal block act separately. To justify the inverse formula, assume every diagonal block is invertible and check both products with the matrix of their inverses. Each diagonal product is an identity and every other block remains zero.

Addition follows by adding corresponding entries. For multiplication, a diagonal block has only one possibly nonzero term, A sub i times B sub i. Every off-diagonal block is zero. Finally, multiply A by the proposed inverse in either order. Every diagonal block becomes the identity of order n sub i, and every off-diagonal block remains zero. The result is the identity matrix of order n sub one plus n sub two, and so on, plus n sub ell. This proves the inverse formula.
原书的“准对角矩阵”通常读作“block diagonal matrix”。指着对角上的各块说明尺寸；不要把准对角矩阵说成只有数值对角元非零。

title: The three types of elementary matrices
zh: 定义10：三类初等矩阵

blocks.text: We now connect elementary operations with matrix multiplication. First, let us define an elementary matrix.
We now define elementary matrices by applying one elementary operation to an identity matrix.
Definition 10. An elementary matrix is obtained from an identity matrix by one elementary row or column operation.

There are three types. We use the textbook's notation. Here i and j are distinct indices, c is a nonzero scalar, and k is any scalar. The order of each matrix is determined by the identity matrix we start with.
Exchanging rows i and j of E gives P(i,j). Multiplying row i by c gives P(i(c)). Adding k times row j to row i gives P(i,j(k)).

In the first matrix, the entries at positions i, i and j, j become zero. The entries at i, j and j, i become one. All other entries stay as in E. In the second matrix, only the diagonal entry at i, i changes, from one to c.

In the third matrix, the entry at i, j is k. All other entries stay as in E. The displayed form assumes i is less than j. If i is greater than j, the k is below the diagonal. Blank positions in these displays are zero.

Read P of i, j for the exchange matrix. For the other two, it is clearer to say “the matrix that scales row i by c,” and “the matrix that adds k times row j to row i.” The parentheses describe an operation; i(c) is not a product.
Column operations on E give the same three types of matrices. In particular, adding k times column i to column j also gives P of i, j of k.
先在板书写E，再只改动相应位置；标出第i、j行列。P(i,j(k))中的k在(i,j)位置。记号P是矩阵名称，不是此处的数域名称。

title: Elementary operations as multiplication
zh: 引理：左乘行变换，右乘列变换

blocks.text: Next, let us state the basic lemma.

An elementary row operation on an s by n matrix A is the same as multiplying A on the left by the corresponding s by s elementary matrix. An elementary column operation is the same as multiplying on the right by the corresponding n by n elementary matrix.

blocks.latex: \text{row operation: }A\longmapsto PA,\quad P:s\times s;\qquad\text{column operation: }A\longmapsto AQ,\quad Q:n\times n.

blocks.text: Proof

We must identify the effect of multiplication for each of the three elementary matrices. On the left, compare rows of the product with rows of A. On the right, compare columns instead. The order of the elementary matrix is fixed by the side on which it acts.
Following the textbook, let A sub one through A sub s denote the rows of A. Let B be any s by s matrix. Block multiplication gives the following expression.

First, set B equal to P of i, j. Row i selects A sub j, and row j selects A sub i. All other rows stay the same. Next, use the scaling matrix. Only row i is multiplied by c. Finally, use the row addition matrix. Only row i changes, to A sub i plus k A sub j.

These are exactly the three row operations. For columns, let C sub one through C sub n be the columns of A. In A Q, column j is the linear combination of these columns with coefficients from column j of Q. This gives the corresponding column operations.

blocks.latex: AP(i,j):\ C_i\leftrightarrow C_j,\qquad AP(i(c)):\ C_i\longmapsto cC_i,\qquad AP(i,j(k)):\ C_j\longmapsto C_j+kC_i.

blocks.text: Notice the last formula. On the left, P of i, j of k changes row i. On the right, it changes column j. The position of k in the elementary matrix explains this difference. This proves the lemma.
行向量的竖排板书沿用原书，明确标出被替换的行。最后列变换公式最容易说反：右乘P(i,j(k))把第i列的k倍加到第j列。

title: Inverses and matrix equivalence
zh: 初等矩阵的逆与定义11：矩阵等价

blocks.text: Each elementary operation can be undone. This gives the inverses of the three elementary matrices.
Every elementary matrix is invertible, and its inverse is also elementary.
Proof

For each elementary matrix, we need another elementary matrix whose product with it is E in both orders. Construct it by undoing the original operation. The scaling operation requires a nonzero scalar so that its reciprocal exists.

Exchange the same two rows again to undo an exchange. Multiply by one over c to undo multiplication by c. Add negative k times row j to row i to undo addition of k times row j. In each case, applying the two operations to E restores E. By the lemma, the corresponding matrix products, in either order, equal E. These are therefore the inverse matrices.
Read c to the minus one as “one over c.” This is defined because c is nonzero. Next, we define matrix equivalence.
We now define equivalence of matrices through sequences of elementary operations.
Definition 11. Matrices A and B are equivalent if B can be obtained from A by a finite sequence of elementary row and column operations.

blocks.latex: A\ \xrightarrow{\text{elementary row and column operations}}\ B.

blocks.text: Reflexivity means every matrix is equivalent to itself. Symmetry means that if A is equivalent to B, then B is equivalent to A. Transitivity means that if A is equivalent to B and B is equivalent to C, then A is equivalent to C.
Proof
Reflexivity

Start with any matrix A. A sequence with no operations already leaves A unchanged, so A is equivalent to itself. If a nonempty sequence is desired, an operation followed by its inverse also returns A.
Symmetry

Assume a finite sequence takes A to B. To take B back to A, undo the last operation first, then undo the preceding operations in reverse order. Each inverse operation is elementary, as proved above. This constructs a valid sequence from B to A.
Transitivity

Assume one finite sequence takes A to B and a second takes B to C. Apply the first sequence and then the second. The combined sequence is still finite and consists of elementary operations, and it takes A to C. This is precisely the definition of their equivalence.
等价允许行和列两类初等变换。自反性说明返回自身的操作；对称性须倒序撤销操作；传递性须连接两段有限操作。

title: The standard form of a matrix
zh: 定理5：矩阵标准形及构造证明

blocks.text: We now show how far elementary operations can simplify a matrix.
Theorem 5. Every s by n matrix A is equivalent to a matrix with r ones at the start of the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere, where r is the rank of A. This is the standard form of A.
If r is zero, the standard form is the zero matrix. If a block has zero rows or columns, we simply omit it. The standard form has the same size as A.
Proof

Let r be the rank of A. We must construct elementary operations giving an identity block and zeros elsewhere. At each step, move a nonzero entry to the upper left of the remaining block, clear its column and row, and scale it to one. Finally, rank invariance will identify the number of ones as r.

If A is zero, it is already in standard form. Otherwise, move a nonzero entry to the upper left corner by row and column exchanges. Call the entries of this current matrix a sub i j. Thus a sub one one is nonzero.
From row i, subtract a sub i one over a sub one one times the first row. This makes every entry below the first entry in column one equal to zero.

From column j, subtract a sub one j over a sub one one times the current first column. Since the current first column is zero below its first entry, this clears the rest of the first row without changing the lower right part. Then multiply the first row by one over a sub one one.

Repeat the process inside A sub one. Operations confined to this smaller block preserve the first diagonal one and the surrounding zeros. Continue until the remaining block is zero or has no rows or columns. We reach the stated form. Its rank is the number of diagonal ones. Elementary operations preserve rank, so this number equals the rank of the original A. This proves the theorem.
A₁在这里表示右下角子矩阵，不是上一引理中的第一行。强调“current first column”，因为消行之后它已变为(a₁₁,0,…,0)ᵀ。

title: Invertible matrices as products of elementary matrices
zh: 定理6：可逆矩阵的初等矩阵分解

blocks.text: The standard form gives a useful description of every invertible matrix.
Theorem 6. A square matrix A is invertible if and only if it is a product of elementary matrices.

blocks.latex: A\text{ invertible}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A=Q_1Q_2\cdots Q_m,\qquad Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\text{ elementary}.

blocks.text: The subscripts label different factors. Read the product as “Q sub one times Q sub two, and so on, times Q sub m.”
Proof

First assume A is a product of elementary matrices. Since each factor is invertible, the product is invertible. For the reverse direction, assume A is invertible and use the standard-form theorem to reduce it to E. Translate those operations into matrix factors and solve for A using their inverses.

First, every elementary matrix is invertible. A product of invertible matrices is invertible, so the displayed product is invertible. Conversely, let A be invertible of order n. Its rank is n. By Theorem Five, its standard form is E. The lemma expresses the operations taking A to E as multiplication by elementary matrices on the left and right.
Here P sub one acts first on the left. R sub one acts first on the right. Multiply by the inverse products to solve for A. Keep the order shown on the board.
Each inverse in this expression is elementary. After omitting E, A is a product of elementary matrices, as required. This proves both directions.
原书通过等价式直接得出定理；此处展开两边乘逆矩阵的顺序。若某侧没有变换，该侧的乘积就是E。

title: Equivalence and invertible factors
zh: 推论1：等价矩阵的乘法表示

blocks.text: Next, let us state the first corollary.
Corollary 1. Two s by n matrices A and B are equivalent if and only if there are an invertible s by s matrix P and an invertible n by n matrix Q such that A = PBQ.

blocks.latex: A\text{ equivalent to }B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A=PBQ,\qquad P:s\times s,\quad Q:n\times n,\quad P,Q\text{ invertible}.

blocks.text: Proof

First assume equivalence by elementary operations and collect the left factors into one invertible matrix and the right factors into another. Conversely, assume the stated factorization and express its invertible factors as products of elementary matrices. This recovers a sequence of allowed operations.

Suppose A and B are equivalent. Since operations can be reversed, we can obtain A from B. By the lemma, each row operation is left multiplication by an elementary matrix, and each column operation is right multiplication by an elementary matrix. Group all left factors into P and all right factors into Q. Associativity allows this grouping, and both products are invertible. Hence A equals P B Q.

Conversely, suppose A equals P B Q with P and Q invertible. By Theorem Six, both P and Q are products of elementary matrices. Multiplying B by these factors performs a sequence of elementary row and column operations. Thus B can be transformed into A, so A and B are equivalent.
此处P、Q的阶数可以不同；必须分别匹配B的行数、列数。不要把A=PBQ当作只适用于方阵的相似关系。

title: Reducing an invertible matrix to the identity
zh: 推论2：仅用行变换化为单位矩阵

blocks.text: The next corollary is stronger than reduction using both rows and columns.
Corollary 2. Every invertible matrix can be reduced to the identity matrix using only elementary row operations.
Proof

Assume A is invertible. By the preceding theorem, write A as a product of elementary matrices. Our target is a sequence using row operations alone. We will remove the factors one at a time by left multiplication with their inverses; each such multiplication is a row operation.
By Theorem Six, write A as a product of elementary matrices. Multiply on the left by their inverses in the following order.

Q sub one inverse acts first and removes the first factor. Then Q sub two inverse acts, and so on. Every inverse is elementary, and every left multiplication is a row operation. Thus row operations alone reduce A to E.
The column version also holds. Multiply the same factorization on the right by the inverse factors, starting with Q sub m inverse.
Each right multiplication is a column operation. Thus an invertible matrix can also be reduced to E using only column operations.
左边连乘写在纸上的顺序与执行顺序相反：最靠近A的Q₁⁻¹先执行。右乘时最靠近A的Q_m⁻¹先执行。

title: Finding an inverse by elementary operations
zh: 用增广矩阵求逆及其证明

blocks.text: We now obtain a practical method for finding the inverse.
If elementary row operations transform an invertible matrix A into E, then applying exactly the same operations to E transforms it into A⁻¹.
Place A and E side by side. This gives an n by two n matrix. Read the display as “the augmented matrix A, E is transformed into E, A inverse.” Apply each row operation across both halves.
Proof

Assume a sequence of row operations changes A into E. Let P be the product of their elementary matrices in the order in which they act. Then PA equals E, so P is A inverse. Applying the very same operations to E produces PE, which is P itself.
Let P sub one through P sub m be the elementary matrices for the row operations, in the order in which we perform them. Then their product, with the last operation on the left, takes A to E.
Therefore the same product takes E to A inverse. Block multiplication combines the two calculations into one.

blocks.latex: P_m\cdots P_1(A\ \ E)=(P_m\cdots P_1A\ \ P_m\cdots P_1E)=(E\ \ A^{-1}).

blocks.text: This proves the method. During the calculation, the left and right halves are the current transformed matrices. We must apply every new row operation to both current halves. Once the left half is E, the right half is the inverse.
For the column-operation version, place A above E and apply the same column operations to both blocks.
Proof

If the column operations give a product Q such that A Q equals E, then Q equals A inverse. Right multiplication of both vertical blocks by Q therefore gives E above A inverse. This proves the column version.
行变换法横向拼接(A E)；列变换法纵向拼接。不要在横向拼接的矩阵中任意使用列变换，否则右半部不再保证是逆矩阵。

title: Elementary operations on blocks
zh: 分块初等变换及乘法公式

blocks.text: Each block operation must be checked with its multiplication side and its block sizes. For addition of one block row to another, choose the multiplier so the two rows have equal heights after multiplication. The block matrix representing the operation then gives the desired new row by the usual product rule.
We now combine block multiplication with elementary operations. Let A and B form the first block row, and C and D the second. The two block rows have m and n rows, respectively.

Compatible block matrices can exchange block rows, multiply a block row on the left by a matrix, or add a matrix multiple of one block row to another. Each operation is represented by block multiplication.

This matrix exchanges the two block rows. Its first block row has n rows and selects the original second block row. Its second block row has m rows and selects the original first block row. Thus m and n need not be equal.
This multiplies the first block row on the left by P. To make the operation reversible, P must be invertible. The identity itself holds for any P of the stated size.
Verification

Apply the block row-by-column rule to each product. In the last formula, the lower left block is P A plus C. The lower right block is P B plus D. This adds P times the first block row to the second block row. The inverse operation uses negative P.

Right multiplication gives the corresponding operations on block columns. Keep the multiplier on the right of each block. For example, if the two block columns have m and n columns, then the following formula holds.
每条公式中的P尺寸按该条公式确定。block row读“块行”；左乘产生PA，右乘产生AP，不能互换。块行交换矩阵上下两块的行数可能不同。

title: Eliminating an off-diagonal block
zh: 分块消元与例1的求逆证明

blocks.text: We next choose the multiplier so that an entire block becomes zero.
If A is invertible, adding −CA⁻¹ times the first block row to the second eliminates C.
Proof

Assume A is invertible. We want to clear the lower left block C while preserving the information in the matrix. Multiplying the first block row on the left by minus C A inverse produces minus C in that position; adding it to the second block row cancels C.

Here A has order m, D has order n, B is m by n, and C is n by m. The new lower left block is C minus C A inverse A, which is zero. The new lower right block is D minus C A inverse B. Read it as “D minus C times A inverse times B.”
Let us apply this to the block triangular matrix in Example One.
Example 1. If A and D are invertible, then T has the following inverse.
Proof
The same elimination turns T into a block diagonal matrix.
Multiply on the left by the inverse of this block diagonal matrix. The total left multiplier takes T to E, so it is T inverse.
This recovers the earlier formula by a different argument: first eliminate the lower left block, then invert the two diagonal blocks.
先写消元矩阵，再写它与T的乘积，最后在左侧乘对角块的逆。两个左乘因子的先后次序不可颠倒。

title: Inverse of a general two-by-two block matrix
zh: 例2：一般二乘二分块矩阵求逆

blocks.text: We now consider Example Two, where all four blocks may be nonzero.
Example 2. Suppose T₁ and its square block D are invertible. Then A − BD⁻¹C is invertible, and T₁ has the inverse shown below.
Read T sub one inverse. The repeated expression A minus B D inverse C is a matrix of order m. We keep this expression written out, as in the textbook.
Proof

The hypotheses say that the whole matrix T sub one and its block D are invertible. They do not initially give invertibility of A minus B D inverse C. We must first derive that fact by block elimination, and only then use its inverse in the final formula.
First, eliminate the upper right block. Subtract B D inverse times the second block row from the first.

The left multiplier is invertible: replace its negative block by the positive block to obtain its inverse. Since T sub one is invertible, the product is invertible. Its determinant is the product of the determinants of its two diagonal blocks.
Thus A minus B D inverse C is invertible. Apply Example One to the block triangular matrix. Then multiply its inverse on the right by the elimination matrix.

Block multiplication gives the four blocks in the stated formula. The upper right block has one minus sign. The product in the lower right block has two minus signs, so it is positive. This completes the proof.
长公式可横向滚动。口述时先指认重复出现的(A−BD⁻¹C)⁻¹，读“the inverse of A minus B times D inverse times C”，再逐块说明。这里是整个括号的逆，不是仅C的逆。

title: A block proof of the determinant product rule
zh: 例3：行列式乘法公式的分块证明

blocks.text: Example Three gives another proof of the determinant product rule. We will use block multiplication and determinant-preserving row additions.
Example 3. For square matrices A and B of the same order n, the determinant of AB equals the product of their determinants.
Proof

We will compute the determinant of one block matrix in two ways. Each calculation uses block elimination followed by a triangular determinant. Comparing the two scalar results yields the determinant product formula.
Form the following product. The upper left block becomes A minus A, which is zero.

We must not use the determinant product rule to take the determinant of this product, because that is what we are proving. Instead, express the left multiplier as a sequence of row additions. As in the textbook, let E sub i j be zero except for the entry a sub i j at position i, j. Define P sub i j by the following block matrix.

Left multiplication by P sub i j adds a sub i j times row n plus j to row i. If that coefficient is zero, it does nothing. Each operation preserves the determinant. The lower n rows never change, so performing these operations for all i and j gives the full left multiplier.
Therefore the determinant of the product on the first line equals the determinant of the original block triangular matrix.
Now exchange column one with column n plus one, column two with column n plus two, and so on. There are n column exchanges. The resulting matrix is block triangular.
The determinant of negative E sub n is negative one to the power n. The two sign factors cancel. Comparing the two evaluations gives the desired identity.
本页Eᵢⱼ特指仅(i,j)位置为aᵢⱼ的矩阵，沿用原书，不是该位置为1的常见矩阵单位。证明不能循环调用|UV|=|U||V|；第一步靠逐次加行，最后用此前已证明的块三角行列式公式。

title: Triangularization by block induction
zh: 例4：下三角乘子与归纳证明

blocks.text: The last example uses induction and block elimination. First, let us state the assumption precisely.

Example 4. Let A have order n. Suppose the determinant of its upper left k by k submatrix is nonzero for every k from one through n. Then there is a lower triangular matrix B such that BA is upper triangular.

blocks.latex: \begin{vmatrix}a_{11}&\cdots&a_{1k}\\\vdots&&\vdots\\a_{k1}&\cdots&a_{kk}\end{vmatrix}\ne0\quad(1\le k\le n),\qquad B\text{ lower triangular},\quad BA\text{ upper triangular}.

blocks.text: Upper triangular means all entries below the main diagonal are zero. Lower triangular means all entries above it are zero. These upper left determinants are called leading principal minors.
Proof

The assumption is that every leading principal minor is nonzero. We use induction on the order. Apply the induction hypothesis to the upper left block, then choose the last block row of the multiplier to clear the remaining lower left entries. We must also keep the multiplier lower triangular.
For n equals one, choose B equal to the one by one identity matrix. Now assume the statement holds for order n minus one. Partition A as follows.

Here alpha is a row vector, and beta is a column vector, each with n minus one entries. A sub one satisfies the same assumption. It is invertible, and by induction there is a lower triangular B sub one such that B sub one A sub one is upper triangular.
In this formula E has order n minus one. The first multiplication clears the bottom left block. Now multiply the first block row by B sub one.
This matrix is upper triangular. Combine the two left multipliers to obtain B.
Since B sub one is lower triangular, B is also lower triangular. Its product with A is the upper triangular matrix just displayed. This completes the induction.
alpha读“alpha”，beta读“beta”；αA₁⁻¹β是1×1的数。先写A的分块和尺寸，再依次写两次左乘，最后合并为B。此处A₁不是A的第一行，而是左上角子矩阵。

title: Quadratic forms
zh: 二次型的定义与系数记号

blocks.text: We now begin quadratic forms. We will write them using matrices, then remove the mixed terms by a change of variables.
We now introduce quadratic forms: polynomials whose terms all have total degree two, together with the zero polynomial.
Definition. A quadratic form in n variables over a number field P is a homogeneous polynomial of degree two with coefficients in P. The zero polynomial is included.

Here P is the field of coefficients. Each term has total degree two. A square term is x sub i squared. A mixed term is x sub i times x sub j, with different indices. We write its coefficient as two a sub i j.
This is the expanded form used in the book. There are no constant or linear terms. The factor two will let us use a symmetric matrix.
先写加粗定义，再写展开式；紧凑求和式可辅助解释。f(x₁,…,xₙ)读“f of x sub one through x sub n”；第二个求和读“the sum over all i and j with one less than or equal to i, i less than j, and j less than or equal to n”。P读“capital P”。

title: Linear substitutions
zh: 定义1：线性替换与非退化替换

blocks.text: Next, we define the changes of variables that we will use.
Next, we define linear substitutions and the condition that makes such a substitution nondegenerate.
Definition 1. A linear substitution expresses x one through x n as linear combinations of y one through y n, with coefficients in P. It is nondegenerate if its coefficient determinant is nonzero.

Capital X and capital Y are column vectors of variables. Capital C is the coefficient matrix. We read X equals C Y as: capital X equals capital C times capital Y. Nondegenerate means that C is invertible.
Property. A linear substitution takes a quadratic form to a quadratic form. A nondegenerate substitution can be reversed.
Proof

For the first property, substitute linear expressions into each degree-two term. Every resulting term still has total degree two, or the terms cancel to give the zero form. For reversibility, the coefficient matrix must be invertible, so the new variables can be expressed in the old ones.

Each old variable is a linear combination of the new variables. Each product of two old variables becomes a sum of products of two new variables. So the result is still a quadratic form, possibly zero. If C is invertible, multiplication by C inverse gives the displayed reverse substitution.
注意方向：X是原变量列，Y是新变量列，板书写X=CY。|C|≠0读“the determinant of C is nonzero”；C⁻¹读“C inverse”。

title: The matrix of a quadratic form
zh: 对称矩阵表示及唯一性

blocks.text: Now let us write a quadratic form using a matrix.
We now introduce symmetric matrices and use them to record the coefficients of quadratic forms.

Definition. A matrix A is symmetric if A transpose equals A. The matrix of a quadratic form is the symmetric matrix whose diagonal entries are the square coefficients and whose off-diagonal entries are half the mixed-term coefficients.
Property. Every quadratic form has a unique symmetric matrix A such that f equals X transpose A X. Conversely, every symmetric matrix defines a quadratic form by this formula.

We read this as: f of x sub one through x sub n equals X transpose times A times X. The superscript T means transpose, not a power. The product is a one by one matrix, which we identify with its entry.
Proof

We must check both existence and uniqueness of a symmetric coefficient matrix. A diagonal entry contributes once to its square term. An off-diagonal entry contributes twice because the matrix is symmetric. Matching the polynomial coefficients therefore determines every entry.
For different i and j, the two terms combine because A is symmetric.

Thus the product gives exactly the original quadratic form. Conversely, the product from any symmetric A has this form. For uniqueness, compare coefficients. The coefficient of x sub i squared determines a sub i i. Half the coefficient of x sub i times x sub j determines a sub i j. Therefore the symmetric matrix is uniquely determined.

blocks.latex: X^{\mathsf T}AX=X^{\mathsf T}BX\text{ as polynomials},\quad A^{\mathsf T}=A,\ B^{\mathsf T}=B\quad\Longrightarrow\quad A=B.

blocks.text: 先指对角元，再指关于主对角线成对的两个位置。唯一性要求A、B都对称，等式是多项式恒等式，不是某一组X的取值相等。

title: Congruence of matrices
zh: 替换公式与定义2：矩阵合同

blocks.text: We now find the matrix after a change of variables.
Property. Under the substitution X equals C Y, a quadratic form with symmetric matrix A has symmetric matrix C transpose A C in the new variables.

blocks.latex: f=X^{\mathsf T}AX,\quad X=CY\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f=Y^{\mathsf T}BY,\qquad B=C^{\mathsf T}AC.

blocks.text: Proof

Assume f has symmetric matrix A and substitute X equals C Y. Our goal is to identify the symmetric matrix in the new variables. First rewrite the expression as Y transpose times a matrix times Y; then check that this middle matrix is symmetric.

blocks.latex: X^{\mathsf T}AX=(CY)^{\mathsf T}A(CY)=Y^{\mathsf T}C^{\mathsf T}ACY=Y^{\mathsf T}(C^{\mathsf T}AC)Y.

blocks.text: We substitute C Y for X. Transposing a product reverses its order. We must also check that the middle matrix is symmetric.
The uniqueness of the symmetric matrix now gives B equals C transpose A C.
The substitution formula suggests a relation between matrices. We now define this relation, called congruence.
Definition 2. Two n by n matrices A and B over P are congruent if there is an invertible n by n matrix C over P such that B equals C transpose A C. This change is called a congruence transformation.
Here A is the original matrix and B is the new matrix. Congruent here describes matrices. It does not mean congruent modulo a number.

Property. Every matrix is congruent to itself. If A is congruent to B, then B is congruent to A. If A is congruent to A sub one and A sub one is congruent to A sub two, then A is congruent to A sub two. These are reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity of congruence.
Proof
First, every matrix is congruent to itself. Choose the identity matrix E.

For symmetry, assume B equals C transpose A C with C invertible. Our target is an invertible matrix expressing A as a congruence of B. Multiply on the left by the transpose of C inverse and on the right by C inverse. This isolates A, and C inverse is itself invertible.

For transitivity, assume A sub one equals C sub one transpose A C sub one, and A sub two equals C sub two transpose A sub one C sub two, with both substitution matrices invertible. Substitute the first equality into the second. The transpose product law combines the two left factors, giving a single congruence with substitution matrix C sub one C sub two.

blocks.latex: A_1=C_1^{\mathsf T}AC_1,\quad A_2=C_2^{\mathsf T}A_1C_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad A_2=(C_1C_2)^{\mathsf T}A(C_1C_2).

blocks.text: The inverse of an invertible matrix is invertible, and the product of two invertible matrices is invertible. This proves all three properties.
B=CᵀAC读“B equals C transpose times A times C”；(C⁻¹)ᵀ读“the transpose of C inverse”。板书依次写自反、对称、传递的等式；不要把左侧Cᵀ误写成C⁻¹。

title: Reduction to square terms
zh: 定理1：配方法与归纳证明

blocks.text: Next, we show that all mixed terms can be removed.
Theorem 1. Every quadratic form over a number field P can be changed into a sum of square terms by a nondegenerate linear substitution over P.
The coefficients d sub i may be positive, negative, or zero when P is real. The theorem only says that mixed terms disappear. It does not say that the form is a sum of positive squares.
Proof: induction and Case 1

We use induction on the number of variables. The target is a substitution that is invertible and leaves only square terms. When a square coefficient is nonzero, complete that square and reduce the remaining form to one fewer variable. We must check invertibility of the substitution as well as the algebraic identity.

We use induction on the number of variables. For one variable, the form is already a single square term. Assume the result holds for n minus one variables. Write the form with a symmetric coefficient matrix.
First suppose some diagonal coefficient is nonzero. We may exchange variables so that a sub one one is nonzero. Separate all terms containing x sub one, then complete the square.
We add a square and subtract its extra part. The remaining terms contain only x sub two through x sub n. We denote their coefficients by b sub i j.
Now choose y sub one to be the expression inside the first square. Keep the other variables unchanged. On the right, I write the inverse substitution.
This substitution is nondegenerate: its coefficient matrix is triangular with every diagonal entry equal to one. The form becomes
Apply the induction assumption to the last n minus one variables. Following the book, write the new variables z in terms of y. Keep z sub one equal to y sub one.
The last substitution is invertible, so it can also be written with y in terms of z. The two substitutions together are nondegenerate. This proves the first case.
a₁₁⁻¹是数a₁₁的倒数，可读“one over a sub one one”。配方中括号平方读“the square of the expression in parentheses”。先完成配方，再写新旧变量关系，不要跳过减去的平方项。

title: The remaining cases of Theorem 1
zh: 定理1续证：无平方项与零首行

blocks.text: We continue the proof of Theorem One with the remaining cases.
Proof, continued: Case 2

We continue the same induction, now assuming that every square coefficient is zero. If a mixed coefficient is nonzero, the first substitution must create a nonzero square coefficient so that the preceding case applies. If every coefficient is zero, the form is already standard.
Suppose all diagonal coefficients are zero, but some entry in the first row is nonzero. By exchanging variables other than the first, we may assume a sub one two is nonzero.
This substitution is nondegenerate. Its first two by two block has determinant minus two, and all other variables stay unchanged.

The coefficient of z sub one squared is now two a sub one two, which is nonzero. No other term contributes to this square: each other mixed term contains a variable with index at least three. We can therefore apply Case One to the new form.
Proof, continued: Case 3
Finally, suppose the entire first row of coefficients is zero. Symmetry makes the first column zero as well.

The form does not depend on x sub one. Apply induction to the other n minus one variables, and leave the first variable unchanged. The full substitution remains nondegenerate. These cases cover every quadratic form, so the proof is complete.
第二种情形要说明为何其他项不产生z₁²；第三种情形是首行全零，不要求整个矩阵为零。不要把“没有平方项”直接当作“零二次型”。

title: Standard form and diagonal matrices
zh: 定理2与标准形的定义

blocks.text: We can now state the same result in matrix language.
