Theorem 2. Over a number field P, every symmetric matrix is congruent to a diagonal matrix.
Proof

Let A be symmetric and consider its quadratic form. Apply the standard-form theorem to obtain a nondegenerate substitution. The substitution formula says that the new matrix is C transpose A C, and a sum of square terms has a diagonal matrix. This proves the matrix statement.

Start with the quadratic form X transpose A X. Theorem One gives a nondegenerate substitution X equals C Y that removes all mixed terms. The matrix of the resulting form is diagonal. It is also C transpose A C by the substitution formula. This proves the theorem.
We now give a name to the sum-of-squares expression obtained by a nondegenerate substitution: a standard form.
Definition. A standard form of a quadratic form is a sum of square terms obtained from it by a nondegenerate linear substitution.
We say a standard form because this definition does not assert uniqueness. The coefficients are still in P. We will discuss uniqueness in the next section.
CᵀAC读“C transpose times A times C”。用手指向对角元d₁到dₙ，说明它们就是各平方项的系数。standard form读“standard form”；本节不引入特征值或正交变换。

title: Completing the square with matrices
zh: 配方法的矩阵证明：非零首项

blocks.text: The book also writes the completing-square proof in matrix form. This tells us how to construct C.
Construction. If A is symmetric and its first diagonal entry is nonzero, a congruence transformation separates that entry from a symmetric matrix of order n minus one.
Here alpha is a row with n minus one entries. A sub one is the bottom right submatrix. Choose C sub one to be the matrix of the substitution used in the first case.
Proof

Assume the first diagonal entry is nonzero. We will choose an invertible triangular substitution matrix that clears the first row and column outside that entry. The remaining block must be symmetric so that the same procedure can continue on a smaller matrix.
C sub one has determinant one. We multiply on the left by its transpose and on the right by C sub one. The first multiplication clears the bottom left block. The second clears the top right block.
The bottom right block is symmetric and has order n minus one. By induction, choose an invertible G that makes this block diagonal. Denote that diagonal matrix by D.
The required matrix is C equals C sub one times C sub two. It is invertible. Notice that the transpose appears in reverse order on the left.
αᵀα读“alpha transpose times alpha”，它是(n−1)×(n−1)矩阵，不是ααᵀ。O表示相应尺寸的零块；Eₙ₋₁读“the identity matrix of order n minus one”。按三行乘法板书，不直接跳到最终对角块。

title: The other matrix cases
zh: 配方法的矩阵证明：其余情形

blocks.text: If the first diagonal entry is zero, we cannot divide by it. First look for a nonzero diagonal entry elsewhere and move it to the first position by simultaneous row and column exchanges. If none exists but the matrix is nonzero, use a nonzero off-diagonal entry to create a square coefficient.
We finish the matrix construction by handling the cases where the first diagonal entry is zero.
Case 2: another diagonal entry is nonzero
If a sub i i is nonzero, exchange row one with row i, and also column one with column i. Let P of one comma i denote the elementary matrix that exchanges those two positions.

blocks.latex: a_{11}=0,\ a_{ii}\ne0,\qquad C_1=P(1,i),\quad P(1,i)^{\mathsf T}=P(1,i),\qquad C_1^{\mathsf T}AC_1=P(1,i)AP(1,i).

blocks.text: The top left entry is now the original a sub i i. We can apply the preceding construction. The same exchange is needed on both sides to preserve symmetry.
Case 3: all diagonal entries are zero

Suppose some entry a sub one j is nonzero. Exchange positions two and j on both sides to move it to position one two. If j is already two, no exchange is needed. Use A for the matrix after this exchange.
Now use the same sum and difference substitution as in the polynomial proof.
This is the upper left two by two block of C sub one transpose A C sub one. Its first diagonal entry is nonzero, so we are back in the first case.
Case 4: the first row is zero
Symmetry also makes the first column zero. Apply induction to the bottom right submatrix and keep the first coordinate unchanged.

Here D is diagonal. Every step is an invertible congruence transformation. Multiply the successive substitution matrices in their order of use to obtain the full matrix C. This completes the matrix construction.
P(1,i)读“P of one comma i”，并说明它是对换矩阵；与数域P区别。用完交换后，A表示当前矩阵，不能把新的a₁₂与原位置混淆。

title: Rank and the number of square terms
zh: 二次型的秩与非零平方项个数

blocks.text: We have proved that every quadratic form has a standard form. We now ask which parts of that form are uniquely determined.
We now define the rank of a quadratic form through its symmetric matrix.
Definition. The rank of a quadratic form is the rank of its symmetric matrix.
We denote the rank by r. Here rank A means the rank of the matrix A.
Property. A nondegenerate linear substitution preserves the rank of a quadratic form. In every standard form, the number of square terms with nonzero coefficients equals this rank.
Proof

Assume the substitution matrix C is invertible. Both C and its transpose preserve rank under multiplication. Apply that fact to the new matrix C transpose A C. For a diagonal matrix, the rank is exactly the number of its nonzero diagonal entries.
Both C and C transpose are invertible. Multiplication by an invertible matrix does not change rank. This gives the equality on the board.
The matrix of a standard form is diagonal. Its rank is the number of its nonzero diagonal entries. Those entries are exactly the coefficients of the square terms. So their number is always r.

We have placed the nonzero coefficients first. The remaining n minus r variables have coefficient zero. The values of the nonzero coefficients need not be unique: rescaling a variable changes its coefficient. We next choose a normalized form over the complex and real numbers.
rank A读“rank of A”；r读“r”。“nonzero square terms”指系数非零，不是指变量当前取值非零。r=0时二次型为零，没有非零平方项。

title: Canonical form over the complex numbers
zh: 定理3：复二次型的规范形及唯一性

blocks.text: First consider a quadratic form over the complex numbers.
We first introduce the canonical form over the complex numbers.
Definition. The canonical form of a complex quadratic form of rank r is the sum of r squares, each with coefficient one, followed by n minus r zero coefficients.
Theorem 3. Every complex quadratic form can be changed to its canonical form by a nondegenerate complex linear substitution. This canonical form is unique.
Proof

Start with a complex standard form. Each nonzero coefficient has a nonzero square root in the complex field. Rescale the corresponding variable to make that coefficient one. The number of such coefficients is the rank, so rank invariance proves uniqueness of the displayed canonical form.
By Theorem One, we can first obtain a standard form. Place the nonzero coefficients first.
Every nonzero complex number has a nonzero square root. For each d sub i, choose one square root. Use the following substitution.

We read the first equation as: y sub one equals one over a square root of d sub one, times z sub one. All diagonal factors are nonzero, so the substitution is nondegenerate. Each nonzero coefficient becomes one.
The rank r does not change under a nondegenerate substitution. It determines the number of ones and zeros. Therefore the canonical form is unique. The substitution itself need not be unique.
Consequence. Two complex symmetric matrices of the same order are congruent if and only if they have the same rank.

blocks.latex: A^{\mathsf T}=A,\quad B^{\mathsf T}=B,\qquad A\text{ and }B\text{ congruent}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}B.

blocks.text: Proof of the consequence

Congruence preserves rank, so equal rank is necessary. Conversely, if the ranks agree, the two matrices reduce to the same diagonal matrix, with r ones and all other entries zero. By symmetry and transitivity of congruence, the original matrices are congruent.
标准形用“standard form”，规范形用“canonical form”。复数的√dᵢ表示所选的一个平方根，不说“positive square root”。这里是普通转置，不是共轭转置。r=0时规范形为0；r=n时没有尾部零变量。

title: Canonical form over the real numbers
zh: 实二次型规范形的定义与存在性

blocks.text: Now consider the real case. We can rescale a nonzero coefficient to one or minus one, according to its sign.
We now introduce the real canonical form, keeping track of positive and negative square terms separately.
Definition. A canonical form of a real quadratic form is a sum of p positive squares and r minus p negative squares, with all remaining coefficients zero. Here r is the rank.
The letter p counts the positive squares. The number of negative squares is r minus p. If either group is empty, we omit it.
Existence. Every real quadratic form can be changed to a canonical form by a nondegenerate real linear substitution.
Proof

Start with a real standard form. A real rescaling can change a nonzero coefficient to one or minus one according to its sign. It cannot change a negative square coefficient to positive. We therefore normalize the absolute values and then arrange positive, negative, and zero terms in order.

First reduce the form to a standard form. Reorder the variables so that positive coefficients come first, negative coefficients next, and zero coefficients last. Write the magnitudes of all nonzero coefficients as positive numbers d sub i.
Every d sub i now has a positive real square root. Make the following diagonal substitution.
Each diagonal factor is nonzero. A positive coefficient becomes one. A negative coefficient becomes minus one.
This proves existence. Rank already determines r. To prove uniqueness, we still need to show that p is fixed.
p读“p”，与数域的大写P区别。dᵢ在本页全部为正数，负号另外写。读规范形时可说“the sum of the first p squares, minus the sum of the next r minus p squares”。

title: The law of inertia
zh: 定理4：惯性定理及完整反证法

blocks.text: We now prove that the number of positive squares cannot change.
Theorem 4. Every real quadratic form can be changed to a canonical form by a nondegenerate real linear substitution, and this canonical form is unique. This is the law of inertia.
Proof

The remaining issue is uniqueness of the number of positive squares; existence and invariance of rank have already been established. Compare two canonical expressions for the same form. If one has more positive squares, we will choose one set of corresponding variable values that makes the two expressions have incompatible signs.
Existence was proved above. The rank fixes r. Suppose two nondegenerate substitutions give canonical forms with p and q positive squares. We must prove p equals q.
Both expressions give the same original quadratic form. Since B Y equals C Z, the new variables are related as follows.
Here capital G is the matrix that expresses Z in terms of Y. We read C inverse B as C inverse times B. In coordinates, this relation is

Assume, for a contradiction, that p is greater than q. We will choose Y so that the left side is positive but the right side is nonpositive. Set the first q coordinates of Z to zero. Also set y sub p plus one through y sub n to zero. This gives the homogeneous system
There are n unknowns. Count the equations: q from the first group, and n minus p from the second group.
A homogeneous system with fewer equations than unknowns has a nonzero solution. Let k sub one through k sub n be such a solution. The last equations force the following values.
At least one of the first p entries is therefore nonzero. Substitute these values into the left side of the identity. Its value is strictly positive.
For the right side, compute Z from these same values using Z equals G Y. The first q equations make z sub one through z sub q zero. The value on the right is therefore nonpositive.

The same identity cannot have a positive value on the left and a nonpositive value on the right. This is a contradiction. Hence p is at most q. Interchanging the two canonical forms gives q at most p. Therefore p equals q. Together with the fixed rank r, this proves uniqueness.
q+(n−p)<n读“q plus n minus p is less than n”。≤0读“is less than or equal to zero”或“is nonpositive”。强调两边使用同一组Y及其对应Z，不能分别任取。q=0时第一组方程为空；p=n时第二组为空，计数与论证仍成立。

title: Inertia indices and signature
zh: 定义3：惯性指数与符号差

blocks.text: The law of inertia lets us give names to the numbers that remain fixed.
The law of inertia lets us define three quantities: the positive index, the negative index, and the signature.

Definition 3. For a real quadratic form of rank r, the number p of positive squares in its canonical form is its positive index of inertia. The number r minus p of negative squares is its negative index of inertia. Their difference, two p minus r, is its signature.
We read the last expression as: two p minus r. Here signature means the difference of the two indices, as in the book.
Property. In any real standard form, the number of positive coefficients is the positive index of inertia, and the number of negative coefficients is the negative index of inertia.
Proof

In a real standard form, rescaling a variable by a nonzero real number multiplies its square coefficient by a positive number. Thus normalization preserves each nonzero sign. The law of inertia makes the resulting positive and negative counts independent of the chosen substitution.

To pass from a real standard form to a canonical form, we divide each variable by the positive square root of the magnitude of its coefficient. This changes the magnitudes to one but keeps every sign. Thus the two counts agree with the counts in the canonical form. The law of inertia makes them independent of the chosen standard form.
positive index of inertia：正惯性指数；negative index of inertia：负惯性指数；signature：符号差。负惯性指数r−p本身是非负整数，不是一个负数。这里不另引入p、q表示正负指数，以免与上一证明中q的含义混淆。

title: Canonical forms of symmetric matrices
zh: 定理5：复、实对称矩阵的规范形

blocks.text: Finally, we express these results in matrix language.
Theorem 5, part one. Every complex symmetric matrix A is congruent to a diagonal matrix with r ones and n minus r zeros, where r is the rank of A.
The notation diag means the diagonal matrix with the listed entries. Every entry off the main diagonal is zero. Here C has complex entries.

Theorem 5, part two. Every real symmetric matrix A is congruent over the real numbers to a diagonal matrix with p ones, r minus p minus ones, and n minus r zeros. The counts p and r minus p are uniquely determined.
In this second formula, C is real. There are r minus p entries equal to minus one. The underbraces show how many entries belong to each group. A group with count zero is omitted.
Proof

Apply the canonical-form results to the quadratic form with matrix A. Over the complex numbers, rank determines the number of ones. Over the real numbers, rank and the positive index determine the counts of ones and minus ones. In each case the substitution matrix is invertible, so the matrix relation is a congruence.

Associate A with the quadratic form X transpose A X. In the complex case, apply Theorem Three. In the real case, apply Theorem Four. Under X equals C Y, the new matrix is C transpose A C. The square coefficients in the canonical form give exactly the displayed diagonal entries. Their uniqueness follows from the uniqueness of the canonical form.
We transfer the inertia terminology from quadratic forms to real symmetric matrices.

Definition. The positive and negative indices of inertia of a real symmetric matrix A are the corresponding indices of its quadratic form X transpose A X. The signature of A is their difference, two p minus r.
读第一行可说“C transpose A C is a diagonal matrix with r ones and n minus r zeros”。第二行的负一组说“r minus p entries equal to minus one”，避免连续两个minus造成歧义。复数部分始终使用转置，不加入复共轭。

title: Positive definite quadratic forms
zh: 定义4：正定二次型

blocks.text: We now study positive definite quadratic forms. We will first define positivity, then give tests using inertia and determinants.
We now introduce positive definiteness for a real quadratic form. The defining requirement concerns every nonzero real vector.
Definition 4. A real quadratic form is positive definite if its value is positive at every nonzero real vector.
Nonzero means that the entries are not all zero. It does not mean that every entry must be nonzero. At the zero vector, every quadratic form has value zero.
Property. A diagonal real quadratic form is positive definite if and only if all its coefficients are positive.

blocks.latex: f=d_1x_1^2+\cdots+d_nx_n^2\text{ is positive definite}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_i>0\ (1\le i\le n).

blocks.text: Proof

For a diagonal real form, we must prove both directions of the criterion. First assume all diagonal coefficients are positive. At a nonzero vector, at least one square term is positive and all others are nonnegative. Conversely, if the form is positive definite, taking one coordinate equal to one and the others zero will test the sign of each coefficient.

If every coefficient is positive, each term is nonnegative. At a nonzero vector, at least one square is positive, so the sum is positive. Conversely, set x sub i equal to one and all other variables equal to zero. The value is d sub i. Positive definiteness therefore requires d sub i to be positive for every i.
positive definite读“positive definite”；>0读“is positive”或“is greater than zero”。强调“不全为零”，不能说“all entries are nonzero”。

title: Preserving positive definiteness
zh: 非退化实替换保持正定性

blocks.text: Next, we check what happens under a change of variables.
Property. A nondegenerate real linear substitution preserves positive definiteness in both directions.

blocks.latex: X=CY,\quad |C|\ne0,\qquad g(Y)=f(CY),\qquad f\text{ positive definite}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ g\text{ positive definite}.

blocks.text: The notation g of Y means the new quadratic form in the entries of Y. The original form is f.
Proof

The substitution matrix is real and invertible. The important point is that it sends every nonzero vector to a nonzero vector. Once this is proved, positivity transfers through the equality of the old and new form values. The inverse substitution will give the reverse implication.
Suppose f is positive definite. Take any real values k sub one through k sub n that are not all zero. Let the corresponding original values be c sub one through c sub n.
If all the c entries were zero, the second equation would make all the k entries zero. That is impossible. Hence the c entries are not all zero, and
Thus g is positive definite. For the reverse direction, use the inverse substitution Y equals C inverse X and apply the same argument.
先写两列数值之间的关系，再解释为什么非零不会变成零。此处小写cᵢ是原变量的取值，大写C是替换矩阵。

title: Inertia and positive definite matrices
zh: 定理6、定义5及行列式推论

blocks.text: The preceding result gives a test in terms of inertia.
Theorem 6. A real quadratic form in n variables is positive definite if and only if its positive index of inertia equals n.
Proof

To prove the equivalence, reduce the real form by a nondegenerate substitution. Positive definiteness survives this substitution. We can therefore test the diagonal form: every coefficient must be positive, which is exactly the condition that the positive index equals n.

Reduce f to a standard form by a nondegenerate real substitution. Positivity is preserved. The diagonal form is positive definite exactly when every coefficient is positive. This means there are n positive square terms, so the positive index of inertia is n.
Next, we define a positive definite matrix through its quadratic form.
Definition 5. A real symmetric matrix A is positive definite if the quadratic form X transpose A X is positive definite.

blocks.latex: A^{\mathsf T}=A,\qquad X^{\mathsf T}AX>0\quad\text{for every real }X\ne0.

blocks.text: Consequence. A real symmetric matrix is positive definite if and only if it is congruent over the real numbers to the identity matrix.

blocks.latex: A\text{ positive definite}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A=C^{\mathsf T}EC=C^{\mathsf T}C\text{ for some real invertible }C.

blocks.text: The canonical form has matrix E, the identity matrix. Thus the consequence follows from Theorem Six and the substitution formula. Congruence can be reversed, which lets us write A in the displayed form.
Corollary. The determinant of a positive definite matrix is positive.
Proof of the corollary
C is real and invertible, so its determinant is a nonzero real number. Its square is positive.
X≠0表示列向量非零。|C|²读“the square of the determinant of C”；不要读成绝对值。正定矩阵在本教材中要求实对称，不能只检查行列式大于零。

title: The leading principal minor criterion
zh: 定义6与定理7：必要性

blocks.text: We now give a test directly in terms of the entries of A.
We first define leading principal minors, using the first i rows and the first i columns together.
Definition 6. The leading principal minor of order i is the determinant of the submatrix in the first i rows and first i columns.
We denote this determinant by H sub i. In particular, H sub one is a sub one one, and H sub n is the determinant of A.
Theorem 7. A real quadratic form with symmetric matrix A is positive definite if and only if every leading principal minor of A is positive.

blocks.latex: f=X^{\mathsf T}AX\text{ positive definite}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H_1>0,\ H_2>0,\ldots,H_n>0.

blocks.text: Proof: necessity

For necessity, assume the entire form is positive definite. Fix k and restrict to vectors whose last n minus k coordinates are zero. We must show that this restricted form is positive definite, so that the determinant result for positive definite matrices applies to its matrix.
Suppose f is positive definite. For each k, retain only the first k variables and set all remaining variables to zero.
At any nonzero choice of the first k variables, the full vector with zeros added is still nonzero. Therefore
So f sub k is positive definite. Its matrix is the upper left k by k submatrix of A. The preceding corollary gives
This proves necessity.
leading principal minor：顺序主子式。指向左上角子矩阵，说明行指标和列指标都是1到k。Hᵢ本身是行列式的值，不是子矩阵。

title: Sufficiency of the minor criterion
zh: 定理7续证：完整分块归纳

blocks.text: We now prove the converse in Theorem Seven.
Proof: sufficiency

For sufficiency, our assumption is that every leading principal minor is positive, and our target is positivity at every nonzero vector. The induction hypothesis gives a positive definite upper left block. We will reduce that block to the identity, clear the last off-diagonal blocks, and use the full determinant to control the last scalar.
Assume all leading principal minors are positive. We use induction on n. For n equals one, the condition is a sub one one greater than zero, so the form is positive definite.
Assume the result for order n minus one. Partition A as in the book. Here A sub one is the upper left submatrix, and alpha is the last column above the diagonal entry.

All leading principal minors of A sub one are positive. By induction, A sub one is positive definite. Hence there is a real invertible G such that G transpose A sub one G is the identity. Extend this change to A.
Next, choose C sub two to clear the upper right block. Its transpose clears the lower left block at the same time.
Let C be the product C sub one C sub two. Denote the last scalar entry by a. Both factors are invertible, so C is invertible.
Take determinants. The determinant of A is positive by the last leading-minor condition. This forces a to be positive.
The final diagonal matrix is congruent to the identity. We can see this by writing the factorization using the positive square root of a.
Thus A is congruent to the identity and is positive definite. This completes the induction and the proof of Theorem Seven.
此处α是列向量，与前节配方法中的行向量α区别；写出尺寸(n−1)×1。αᵀGGᵀα是一个数，读“alpha transpose times G times G transpose times alpha”。C₁、C₂按实际次序相乘，不能倒置。

title: Other types of definiteness
zh: 定义7及负定判别

blocks.text: Next, we define negative definiteness, the two semidefinite conditions, and indefiniteness.

Definition 7. A real quadratic form is negative definite if it is negative at every nonzero real vector. It is positive semidefinite if it is nonnegative at every real vector, and negative semidefinite if it is nonpositive at every real vector. It is indefinite if it is neither positive semidefinite nor negative semidefinite.

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}\text{negative definite: }&f(X)<0\quad(X\ne0),\\\text{positive semidefinite: }&f(X)\ge0\quad\text{for all }X,\\\text{negative semidefinite: }&f(X)\le0\quad\text{for all }X,\\\text{indefinite: }&f(U)>0\text{ and }f(V)<0\text{ for some real }U,V.\end{aligned}

blocks.text: Here f of X means f evaluated at the entries of the column vector X. Nonnegative includes zero. An indefinite form takes both positive and negative values. The zero form is both positive semidefinite and negative semidefinite.

Consequence. A real symmetric matrix A defines a negative definite form if and only if its leading principal minors alternate in sign: the odd-order minors are negative and the even-order minors are positive.
Proof

To characterize negative definiteness, apply the positive definite criterion to minus f. Its matrix is minus A. In a minor of order i, each of the i rows acquires a factor minus one, so the determinant acquires the factor minus one to the power i.

The form f is negative definite exactly when minus f is positive definite. The matrix of minus f is minus A. Its leading principal minor of order i is minus one to the power i times H sub i. Apply Theorem Seven to minus A.
positive semidefinite：半正定；negative semidefinite：半负定；indefinite：不定。(-1)ⁱHᵢ读“minus one to the power i times H sub i”。不定不等于“不是正定”。

title: Tests for positive semidefiniteness
zh: 定理8：半正定的五个等价条件

blocks.text: We finish with tests for positive semidefiniteness. A principal minor uses the same set of row indices and column indices. The indices need not be the first consecutive ones.
Theorem 8. Let f equal X transpose A X, with A real symmetric of order n. The following five conditions are equivalent.

1. The form f is positive semidefinite. 2. Its positive index of inertia equals its rank. 3. A is congruent over the real numbers to a diagonal matrix with nonnegative diagonal entries. 4. A equals C transpose C for some real matrix C. 5. Every principal minor of A is nonnegative.

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}(1)\ &X^{\mathsf T}AX\ge0\quad\text{for every real }X;\\(2)\ &p=r;\\(3)\ &C^{\mathsf T}AC=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n),\quad |C|\ne0,\quad d_i\ge0;\\(4)\ &A=C^{\mathsf T}C;\\(5)\ &\det A[I,I]\ge0\quad\text{for every nonempty index set }I.\end{aligned}

blocks.text: Here p is the positive index of inertia and r is the rank. A bracket I comma I means the submatrix using the rows and columns listed in I. The matrix C in condition three must be invertible. The matrix C in condition four need not be invertible. These are separate existence statements and need not use the same matrix.
教材将定理8的证明留作练习。以下两节中的证明是为讲稿补充的，并非原书已有的逐行证明。此处保留正文定理，不加入章后习题。A[I,I]读“the principal submatrix of A on the index set I”。
Supplementary proof: conditions 1 through 4

We first connect conditions one, two, and three by the real canonical form. We then construct a factorization for condition four using square roots of nonnegative diagonal entries, and check directly that such a factorization implies condition one. This will complete the equivalence of the first four conditions.

By the real canonical form, nonnegativity is equivalent to having no negative square terms. This means p equals r. It is also equivalent to a diagonal form with all coefficients nonnegative. This proves the equivalence of the first three conditions.
To obtain condition four from condition three, use a different letter T for the invertible substitution matrix. Take the nonnegative square roots of the diagonal entries.
So choose C equals S times T inverse. Conversely, if A equals C transpose C, its quadratic form is a sum of real squares.
We have constructed a square C of order n. A rectangular real C with n columns also gives a nonnegative sum of squares. This proves condition four implies condition one.

title: Why all principal minors are needed
zh: 定理8续证：主子式与反例

blocks.text: We now prove the part of Theorem Eight concerning all principal minors.
Supplementary proof: condition 1 implies condition 5

For this direction, assume f is positive semidefinite and choose any principal submatrix. Our target is a nonnegative determinant for that submatrix. Restrict f to the corresponding coordinates, then apply its canonical form and the determinant formula for congruence.

Restrict a positive semidefinite form to any selected coordinates, setting the other coordinates to zero. The resulting form is still positive semidefinite. Its symmetric matrix is the corresponding principal submatrix. Its canonical diagonal entries are ones and zeros. Its determinant is therefore nonnegative, since a congruence changes a determinant by a nonzero square. Thus every principal minor is nonnegative.
Supplementary proof: condition 5 implies condition 1

Now assume every principal minor is nonnegative. We must prove that the quadratic form is nonnegative at every real vector. In the induction step, we need a smaller symmetric matrix that retains the same principal-minor condition; the block elimination below constructs exactly that matrix.

We use induction on the order n. The case n equals one is immediate. Assume all principal minors of A are nonnegative. In particular, every diagonal entry is nonnegative. If they are all zero, the two by two principal minors force all other entries to be zero as well.

In this case A is zero and the form is positive semidefinite. Otherwise, exchange the same rows and columns to place a positive diagonal entry first. This only relabels the principal minors. Write the resulting matrix as follows.

Here beta is a row vector, B has order n minus one, and D is symmetric. Select any nonempty set J of indices in B. Write B sub J for that principal submatrix, and beta sub J for the matching entries of beta. Block elimination gives
The determinant on the left is a principal minor of A, so it is nonnegative. Since a is positive, every principal minor of D is nonnegative. By induction, D is positive semidefinite.
Here Z contains the last n minus one variables. Both terms on the right are nonnegative. Hence A defines a positive semidefinite form. This completes the proof of Theorem Eight.
Warning. Nonnegative leading principal minors alone do not imply positive semidefiniteness.
Both leading principal minors are zero, but f at zero comma one equals minus one. The other principal minor of order one is minus one. This is why condition five requires all principal minors.
此补充证明只用归纳、分块消元与配方。β读“beta”；βZ是一个数；Dⱼ是D的对应主子矩阵。最后反例来自正文，必须区分“所有主子式”与“顺序主子式”。

title: Sets, elements, and subsets
zh: 集合、元素、空集与子集

blocks.text: We now begin linear spaces. We first introduce the set and mapping notation used in this chapter.
We first introduce sets, elements, the empty set, equality of sets, and subsets.

Definitions. A set is a collection of objects, called its elements. The empty set has no elements. Two sets are equal if they have exactly the same elements. A set M is a subset of N if every element of M belongs to N.

blocks.latex: a\in M,\quad a\notin M,\quad M=\{a\mid a\text{ has the stated property}\},\quad\varnothing\text{ is the empty set}.

blocks.text: We read a belongs to M, or a is an element of M. The crossed symbol means does not belong to. In braces, the vertical bar means such that. The symbol for the empty set is read the empty set.

blocks.latex: M=N\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (a\in M\ \Longleftrightarrow\ a\in N),\qquad M\subset N\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (a\in M\ \Longrightarrow\ a\in N).

blocks.text: Each condition applies to every a. We read M subset N as M is a subset of N. In this book, this symbol allows equality. A proper subset is a subset that is not equal to the whole set.
Properties. Every set is a subset of itself. The empty set is a subset of every set. Two sets are equal if each is a subset of the other.

blocks.latex: M\subset M,\qquad\varnothing\subset M,\qquad M=N\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (M\subset N\text{ and }N\subset M).

blocks.text: Proof

Each claim is a statement about membership. For an inclusion, start with an arbitrary element of the smaller set and show it belongs to the larger set. For equality, prove this implication in both directions. The empty set has no element that could violate an inclusion.

Every element of M belongs to M, giving the first property. The empty set has no element that could fail to belong to M, giving the second. Finally, the two inclusions say that M and N have exactly the same elements, which is the definition of equality.
保留教材⊂的用法：允许M=N；不要按其他教材的“真子集”习惯误读。∈描述元素属于集合，⊂描述集合包含关系。双向箭头读“if and only if”。

title: Intersection and union
zh: 集合的交与并

blocks.text: We now define intersection and union by stating exactly which elements they contain.
Definitions. The intersection of M and N consists of the elements belonging to both sets. Their union consists of the elements belonging to at least one of the two sets.

blocks.latex: M\cap N=\{a\mid a\in M\text{ and }a\in N\},\qquad M\cup N=\{a\mid a\in M\text{ or }a\in N\}.

blocks.text: We read M intersection N and M union N. Here or includes the case where an element belongs to both sets.
Properties. The intersection is a subset of each set. The union contains each set.

blocks.latex: M\cap N\subset M,\quad M\cap N\subset N,\qquad M\subset M\cup N,\quad N\subset M\cup N.

blocks.text: Proof

To prove each inclusion, take an arbitrary element of its left-hand set. The definition of intersection supplies two membership conditions, while the definition of union requires only one. We will use these conditions to establish membership on the right.

An element of the intersection belongs to both M and N, so the first two inclusions follow. Every element of M belongs to at least one of the two sets, so it belongs to the union. The same argument applies to N.
∩读“intersection”，∪读“union”。这里只需按成员条件证明四个包含关系，不加入额外集合运算法则。

title: Mappings and their values
zh: 映射、像、原像与相等

blocks.text: We first define a mapping and the terms image and preimage.

Definition. A mapping from M to M prime assigns exactly one element of M prime to each element of M. If sigma sends a to a prime, then a prime is the image of a, and a is a preimage of a prime. A mapping from a set to itself is also called a transformation.

We read sigma from M to M prime, and sigma of a equals a prime. A prime is the name of an element here, not a derivative. Each input has exactly one output. Different inputs may still have the same output.
Next, we define when two mappings are equal.
Definition. Two mappings with the same source and target sets are equal if they have the same value at every element of the source set.
We now introduce the identity mapping on a set.
Definition. The identity mapping on M sends every element of M to itself. We denote it by one sub M.
The subscript tells us which set is used. This is a mapping, although its notation uses the number one.

The words each and exactly one are essential. No source element may be left without an image, and one source element cannot be assigned two different images. In contrast, the definition does not require every target element to be reached, and it does not forbid two source elements from sharing an image.
σ读“sigma”，τ读“tau”，M′读“M prime”，a′读“a prime”。image：像；preimage：原像。一个输出可以有多个原像，也可以没有原像。

title: Composition of mappings
zh: 映射乘法、单位律与结合律

blocks.text: Mappings can be applied one after another. The book calls this their product.
We now define the product, or composition, of two mappings with matching source and target sets.
Definition. If sigma maps M to M prime and tau maps M prime to M double prime, their product tau sigma first applies sigma and then tau.
We read tau sigma of a equals tau of sigma of a. The mapping on the right is applied first. This product is composition, not multiplication of two output values.
Properties. Composing with the appropriate identity mapping leaves a mapping unchanged. Composition of mappings is associative.
Proof

Equality of mappings requires the same source and target and equal values at every input. The stated domains make the compositions meaningful. We therefore fix an arbitrary input a and evaluate both sides of each identity at that same a.
For the identity equations, evaluate at any a in M.
For associativity, both sides have source M and target M triple prime. Again compare their values at any a in M.
The values agree for every a, so the two mappings are equal.
ψ读“psi”，M″读“M double prime”，M‴读“M triple prime”。先写集合间的方向，再写复合；τσ从右往左作用，不能按书写顺序先做τ。

title: Injective and surjective mappings
zh: 像集、满射、单射与双射

blocks.text: We now describe whether a mapping reaches every target and whether different inputs stay distinct.
We first define the image set, then introduce surjectivity, injectivity, and bijectivity.

Definitions. The image set sigma of M consists of all outputs of sigma. The mapping is surjective if this image set equals the target set. It is injective if different inputs have different outputs. It is bijective if it is both injective and surjective.
Surjective is also called onto. Injective is also called one-to-one. Bijective is also called a one-to-one correspondence. Equivalently, for an injective mapping, equal outputs force equal inputs.
Property. Two finite sets admit a bijection if and only if they have the same number of elements.
Proof

For finite sets, first assume there is a bijection: injectivity prevents repeated targets and surjectivity leaves none unused. For the converse, assume equal finite counts and construct a pairing. We must check that the pairing is both injective and surjective.

A bijection pairs each source element with one different target element and reaches every target. Thus the counts are equal. Conversely, if the finite counts agree, list the elements of both sets and match entries in the same position.

For infinite sets, a set may admit a bijection with a proper subset. The book gives the integers and the even integers: send n to two n. Different integers give different outputs, and every even integer occurs.
surjective / onto：满射；injective / one-to-one：单射；bijective：双射。σ(M)是像集，通常只是目标集M′的子集。此处是教材正式定义，不将双射概念提前用于旧讲稿的排列计数证明。

title: Inverse mappings
zh: 逆映射与双射的复合

blocks.text: We now define the inverse of a bijective mapping.
Definition. For a bijection sigma from M to M prime, the inverse mapping sends each element of M prime to its unique preimage in M.
We read sigma inverse of a prime equals a. Surjectivity gives a preimage for every target. Injectivity makes that preimage unique, so the inverse is well defined.
Property. The inverse mapping is a bijection and satisfies the two inverse identities.
Proof

Assume sigma is a bijection, so every target element has exactly one preimage. We must check the inverse identities and then both defining conditions for the inverse to be a bijection. Use the original mapping to recover an input whenever two inverse values agree.

Applying sigma and then its inverse returns the original input. Applying the inverse and then sigma returns the original target. These give the two displayed identities. If two inverse images agree, applying sigma shows that their inputs agree, so the inverse is injective. Every a in M is the inverse image of sigma of a, so the inverse is surjective.
Property. The composition of two bijections is a bijection.
Proof
If two outputs of tau sigma agree, injectivity of tau first gives equal outputs of sigma. Injectivity of sigma then gives equal inputs.

For any b in M double prime, surjectivity of tau gives an a prime in M prime with tau of a prime equal to b. Surjectivity of sigma gives an a in M with sigma of a equal to a prime. Hence tau sigma sends a to b. This proves surjectivity and completes the proof.
教材将最后一条证明留给读者，这里补足简短证明。σ⁻¹是逆映射，不是数的倒数；两个单位映射的下标分别为M和M′。

title: The definition of a linear space
zh: 定义1：线性空间的八条公理

blocks.text: We now define a linear space. The objects may be tuples, matrices, polynomials, or functions. What matters is how addition and scalar multiplication behave.
We now state the full definition of a linear space over a number field P.

Definition 1. A linear space over a number field P is a nonempty set V with addition and scalar multiplication. Each sum of two elements of V and each scalar multiple by an element of P is a uniquely defined element of V. The two operations satisfy the following eight rules.

blocks.latex: \alpha,\beta\in V\ \Longrightarrow\ \alpha+\beta\in V,\qquad k\in P,\ \alpha\in V\ \Longrightarrow\ k\alpha\in V.

blocks.text: Elements of V are called vectors. Elements of P are called scalars. We use alpha, beta, and gamma for vectors, and k and l for scalars. The first four rules concern addition.

blocks.latex: \begin{aligned}(1)\quad&\alpha+\beta=\beta+\alpha;\\(2)\quad&(\alpha+\beta)+\gamma=\alpha+(\beta+\gamma);\\(3)\quad&\text{there is }0\in V\text{ such that }0+\alpha=\alpha\text{ for every }\alpha\in V;\\(4)\quad&\text{for each }\alpha\in V\text{ there is }\beta\in V\text{ such that }\alpha+\beta=0.\end{aligned}

blocks.text: The first rule is commutativity. The second is associativity. The third gives a zero vector. The fourth gives an additive inverse for each vector. The next two rules concern scalar multiplication.
Scalar one leaves the vector unchanged. Two successive scalar multiplications agree with multiplication by the product of the scalars. The last two rules are the distributive laws.

The first distributes over a sum of scalars. The second distributes over a sum of vectors. These rules must hold for every choice of the stated vectors and scalars. The zero vector belongs to V; the scalar zero belongs to P.
A linear space is also called a vector space. We will use the following familiar spaces later. Their operations are the usual addition and scalar multiplication.

blocks.latex: P^n=\{(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\mid a_i\in P\},\qquad P^{m\times n}=\{m\times n\text{ matrices over }P\}.
P[x]=\{\text{polynomials in }x\text{ over }P\},\qquad P[x]_n=\{0\}\cup\{f(x)\in P[x]\mid\deg f<n\}.

blocks.text: We read P to the n, P to the m by n, P of x, and P of x sub n. In the last space, the degree is strictly less than n, and the zero polynomial is included. The field P is itself a linear space over P.

For P to the n and the matrix space, addition and scalar multiplication act entry by entry, so the eight rules follow from the field laws. For polynomials, they act on coefficients. Adding two polynomials of degree less than n cannot create a higher-degree term, and multiplying by a scalar also preserves this bound. The zero polynomial is included so that closure and the zero-vector axiom hold.
α、β、γ读“alpha, beta, gamma”；k(lα)读“k times l times alpha”，需指明先做括号内数乘。八条公理须完整板书。P[x]的方括号表示多项式空间，不是代入函数值；deg读“degree”。

title: Uniqueness of zero and additive inverses
zh: 零元素、负元素的唯一性与减法

blocks.text: We now derive simple properties directly from the eight rules.
Property 1. The zero vector of a linear space is unique.
Proof

To prove uniqueness of the zero vector, assume there are two candidates. We must prove that they are the same element. Evaluate their sum using each candidate as the additive identity; the two evaluations give the required equality.
Suppose zero sub one and zero sub two are both zero vectors. Evaluate their sum in two ways. Each acts as an additive identity.
Thus the two zero vectors are equal.
Property 2. Each vector has a unique additive inverse.
Proof
Suppose beta and gamma are both additive inverses of alpha. Use the zero-vector rule, associativity, and commutativity.
This proves uniqueness. We denote the additive inverse of alpha by minus alpha.
With the additive inverse now uniquely determined, we can define vector subtraction.
Definition. Subtraction of vectors is addition of the additive inverse.
additive inverse：加法逆元，教材称负元素。−α读“minus alpha”。证明只用公理，不能先假定减法具有通常性质。

title: Zero products and scalar multiplication

blocks.text: Finally, we prove the basic identities involving zero and scalar multiplication.
Property 3. Scalar zero times any vector is the zero vector. Any scalar times the zero vector is the zero vector. Scalar minus one times a vector is its additive inverse.
In the first equation, the zero on the left is a scalar. In the second, the zero being multiplied is a vector. The result in each case is the zero vector.
Proof

These are consequences of the axioms, so we must derive them without assuming ordinary cancellation in advance. We first prove the scalar-zero identity by distributivity, using addition of an additive inverse to cancel. We can then identify minus one times a vector as its unique additive inverse.
